about: Beyond Chaos CE 6.1.3's junction effects, read from its SNES patches (tables/patch_junction_*.txt) by bc-junction's readers, 2026-11-20. One entry per junction key (index, BC's short name, the patches, the hook, whose junction is checked, trigger, effect, numbers, order against vanilla, notes) and 'patch:<file>' entries for shared code. Group A = damage/elements, B = triggers/procs/commands, C = battle flow. Several keys have parts in two groups (parts[]).

reflect_boost.holder: caster or any reflector: n = number of reflect_boost holders among {the caster} + {every combatant in this cast's reflector set $A6}
reflect_boost.hook: C2/34BB (JSL main + NOP, replaces REP #$20 / LSR $11B0) in C2/3483, the reflected-spell bounce pass that runs after the first pass when $A6 (targets that reflected) is non-zero
reflect_boost.trigger: a non-physical action that bounced off >= 1 target's Reflect (or a Repel junction); once per cast, before the bounced copies resolve
reflect_boost.effect: n = 0: vanilla, bounce uses $11B0/2. n >= 1: no halving; then $11B0 x1.25 for each holder beyond the first.
reflect_boost.numbers: n=0: floor(d/2); n=1: d; n=2: d+floor(d/4); each further holder another x1.25 (floor, saturating 65535)
reflect_boost.order: replaces only the vanilla halving. $11B0 here already contains the first pass's damage_modification boosts, multi-target split and $BC multiplier (crit etc.); the bounce then runs hit/status/C2/0B83 per new target and damage_trigger (X = original caster).
reflect_boost.vanilla_meaning: C2/34BB: halve $11B0 for the bounced copies of a reflected spell
reflect_boost.notes: Caster read from the stack ($06,S = X pushed at C2/3483); reflectors from $04-05,S (the $A6 mask pushed there). A combatant that is both caster and reflector counts once. Also scales reflected healing ($11B0 is the heal base). Uses damage_modification's boost-damage-quarter (62/1440).

null_reflect.hook: C2/2235 (JML main + NOP) in hit determination C2/220D, at the vanilla Reflect test; exits to C2/2241 (reflect) or C2/224B (no reflect, continue: death-protection miss, only-dead check, Interceptor, Faith/hit roll)
null_reflect.trigger: every target check of every action by the holder
null_reflect.effect: the holder's actions are never reflected: skips Repel <element>, Repel Nuke and the vanilla Reflect test for every target; the action continues as if the target had no Reflect.
null_reflect.order: first test in the repel patch's main, before the physical/DoT exclusions, Prism Wall, Repel checks and vanilla Reflect
null_reflect.vanilla_meaning: C2/2235: if not unreflectable ($11A3 b1) and target has Reflect ($3EF8 b7): add target to $A6, miss here (bounced later by C2/3483)
null_reflect.notes: X = attacker in the normal pass. In the bounce pass (C2/34EB calls C2/220D) X is the reflector and Y the new target, so there the reflector's Null Reflect is the one tested (vanilla bounced copies are unreflectable, but Repel ignores that flag).

repel_fire.hook: C2/2235 (JML main) in hit determination C2/220D, replacing the vanilla Reflect test
repel_fire.trigger: per target: attacker lacks Null Reflect; action not physical ($11A2 b0); not a DoT tick; and the element mask contains Fire ($01). Element mask = $11A1 (including EspAtk-added esper elements), or for a non-elemental 'ignore defense' attack a random element rolled by Prism Wall (see prism_wall).
repel_fire.effect: if the target has Repel Fire, the action is reflected exactly like Reflect: $BA b7 ('abort on allies') cleared, target added to $A6, this target is missed; C2/3483 later bounces it at a random combatant opposite the reflector (normally the caster's side) (half damage unless Rflect Boost). Needs no Reflect status and ignores the 'unreflectable' flag ($11A3 b1).
repel_fire.order: Repel checks in order Fire, Ice, Bolt, Bio, Wind, Pearl, Earth, Water; first match reflects; only if none matches is the vanilla Reflect test done. All before death protection, Faith and the hit roll.
repel_fire.notes: 'DoT tick' = jun-check-is-damage-over-time: self-targeted action (attacker == Y) with $3A7C = $22 and $B5 = $12, i.e. the periodic Poison/Regen/Seizure-type status tick. Repel never applies to physical attacks. Multi-element attack: any one matching Repel reflects it. In the bounce pass the bounced copy is tested again (X = reflector): a Repel holder on the caster's side then 'reflects' it again, which there only means it misses that holder ($A6 is not processed a second time). Spells vanilla can't reflect (unreflectable flag) are repelled too.

repel_ice.order: as repel_fire (checked in the fixed order Fire..Water)

repel_bolt.order: as repel_fire (checked in the fixed order Fire..Water)

repel_poison.order: as repel_fire (checked in the fixed order Fire..Water)

repel_nuke.holder: target for 'ignore defense' attacks; the ATTACKER for other attacks (register bug, see notes)
repel_nuke.trigger: non-elemental ($11A1 = 0 and Prism Wall did not roll an element), not physical, $11A4 b0 (heal) and b7 (%HP) clear, power $11A6 != 0, attacker lacks Null Reflect, not a DoT tick
repel_nuke.effect: if the tested combatant has Repel Nuke, the action is reflected as in repel_fire (no Reflect needed, unreflectable ignored)
repel_nuke.order: only reached when Prism Wall gave no element; then this check, then vanilla Reflect test
repel_nuke.notes: Bug: X only becomes the target through check-prism's TYX, which happens only when the attack has $11A2 b5 ('ignore defense') and the attacker lacks Prism Wall. For non-elemental spells without ignore-defense X is still the attacker, so the CASTER's Repel Nuke is tested and such a caster has every such spell bounced off every target. Intended holder is presumably the target; port decision needed. Banned from espers and equipment (esper_banlist/equip_banlist). 'Nuke' here differs slightly from boost_nuke (adds power != 0).

prism_wall.holder: attacker or target (attacker checked first, then target)
prism_wall.hook: check-prism (62/13C0), called from the repel main (C2/2235) and the pierce main (C2/0BD3)
prism_wall.trigger: attack with no element ($11A1 = 0) and 'ignore defense' ($11A2 b5)
prism_wall.effect: one random element is rolled (jun-rng2 & 7 -> one of the 8 bits, equal odds). Repel patch: that element is used for the target's Repel <element> checks (non-physical, non-DoT, attacker without Null Reflect), and the Repel Nuke check is skipped. Pierce patch: the rolled element is only used to choose the 'elemental' path and then discarded - with $11A1 = 0 nothing changes (no absorb/null/half/weak, no damage change).
prism_wall.order: repel: before the element Repel checks; pierce: after Art License/EspAtk, before the pierce checks
prism_wall.notes: In CE 6.1.3 the attack never actually becomes elemental (damage_modification and vanilla element tests never see the roll), so Prism Wall alone does nothing; only with Repel junctions on the target does it matter (each Repel element = 1/8 chance to bounce a non-elemental defense-ignoring spell). Two independent rolls (repel and pierce) per target; the pierce roll only consumes RNG.

boost_fire.hook: C2/336F (JML main; main re-executes the replaced LDA $11A2 / LSR and returns to C2/3373). Per-strike combat routine (C2/3292 path), X = attacker, $11B0 = this strike's base damage/healing (from C2/2B9D), $11A1 = attack elements. Runs after Morph's $BC+=2, before Berserk's $BC+=1. -> check-element(J:boost_fire)
boost_fire.trigger: strike whose element byte $11A1 has Fire ($01) (after EspAtk may have added the equipped esper's elements); damage or healing
boost_fire.effect: if the attacker has Fire Boost: $11B0 x1.5. Then, independent of the attacker, Fire Font (x1.25 per living holder) and Fire Sink (x0.75 per living holder) are applied (see fire_font / fire_sink).
boost_fire.order: per element: boost -> fonts -> sinks; elements in order Fire, Ice, Bolt, Bio, Wind, Pearl, Earth, Water; a multi-element attack gets every matching element's modifiers, multiplied in that order. damage_modification order (all on $11B0, once per strike): 1 EspAtk adds esper elements to $11A1; 2 for each element in $11A1 in order Fire, Ice, Bolt, Bio, Wind, Pearl, Earth, Water: attacker's <elem> Boost x1.5, then x1.25 per living <elem> Font holder, then x0.75 per living <elem> Sink holder; 3 Summon Boost; 4 Nuke Boost/Font/Sink; 5 Phys Boost/Font/Sink; 6 Loner; 7 Crisis Arm; 8 Gaia Boost; 9 Atma Force. Then vanilla: Berserk $BC+1, multi-target split /2 (C2/337E), back-row /2 (C2/3392), special-effect pre-hook C2/3E7D, hit checks, crit ($BC+2, Crit Boost), $11B0 x(1+$BC/2) at C2/341C, then per target C2/0B83 (variance, defense, Safe/Shell, elements w/ pierce), then damage_trigger.
boost_fire.notes: Shared mechanism for the element family: junction index & 7 -> element bit through the C0/BAFC table (01 Fire, 02 Ice, 04 Bolt, 08 Poison/Bio, 10 Wind, 20 Pearl, 40 Earth, 80 Water); font index = (boost index & 7) + J:fire_font, sink index = (boost index & 7) + J:fire_sink. Applies per strike, before multi-target split, crit/$BC, variance, defense and the target's weakness/absorb. X = attacker (for Sketch, the sketcher).

fire_font.holder: any living combatant (both sides; count of holders)
fire_font.hook: C2/336F damage_modification main (X = attacker, on $11B0 before split/crit/defense) -> check-element -> jun-check-count-all-living((boost idx & 7) + J:fire_font)
fire_font.trigger: any strike, by anyone, whose $11A1 has Fire ($01)
fire_font.effect: $11B0 x1.25 once per living Fire Font holder (n holders -> n times)
fire_font.numbers: x1.25 = d + floor(d/4), saturating at 65535; e.g. 2 holders: x1.5625 (floored twice)
fire_font.order: inside the Fire step: attacker's Fire Boost -> Fire Font(s) -> Fire Sink(s); then the next element. full damage_modification order: see patch:patch_junction_damage_modification.txt
fire_font.notes: The manifest's patch_list has no entry for fire_font, but damage_modification reaches index 0x60 by arithmetic ((J:boost_fire & 7) + J:fire_font) and every junction patch is always written (enable_all_patches), so Fire Font works like the other fonts. 'living' = jun-check-entity-living: character bit in $3A74 and not Wound ($3EE4 b7) and not Hidden ($3EF9 b5); monster bit in $3A75. Count covers all 10 slots, both sides (attacker, targets, bystanders); each holder's check is a separate jun-checker call (each can be cancelled by Junction Jammer). Holders boost their enemies' Fire attacks too. Applies to Fire-element healing as well.

fire_sink.notes: 'living' = jun-check-entity-living: character bit in $3A74 and not Wound ($3EE4 b7) and not Hidden ($3EF9 b5); monster bit in $3A75. pierce_fire.hook: C2/0BD3 (JML main + NOP, replaces LDA $11A1 / BEQ $0C1E) in per-target damage modification C2/0B83, element section; plus C2/0BD8 (JML fix-force-field) and C2/0BE5 / C2/0BF5 / C2/0C03 where BIT $11A1 becomes BIT $10
pierce_fire.trigger: per target: attack with power ($11A6 != 0), target not Petrified, $11A1 contains Fire
pierce_fire.effect: builds the 'resistable elements' mask $10 = $11A1; if the attacker has Fire Pierce, Fire is removed from $10. The target's absorb ($3BCC), nullify ($3BCD) and half ($3BE1) tests use $10, so Fire can't be absorbed, nullified or halved. Weakness ($3BE0, x2) still tests the full $11A1 and ForceField ($3EC8) still nullifies (fix-force-field tests $11A1|$10 = $11A1, i.e. unchanged).
pierce_fire.order: per target after variance/defense/Safe/Shell (C2/0C9E) and the undead/heal-flag setup; vanilla precedence absorb > null > half > weak remains, evaluated on $10. Mask built: Art License (clears all) -> EspAtk (removes esper elements) -> Prism Wall roll (discarded) -> pierces Fire..Water.
pierce_fire.vanilla_meaning: C2/0BD3: if no element skip; ForceField nullify; absorb (toggle heal), else null (0), else half, else weak (x2, if < 32768)
pierce_fire.notes: Shared mechanism for the pierce family (index & 7 -> element bit). Multi-element attacks: each element needs its own pierce; an unpierced element can still be absorbed/nulled/halved (vanilla any-bit test). In the reflect bounce pass X is the reflector, so the reflector's pierce is tested.

pierce_ice.effect: as pierce_fire: Ice can't be absorbed, nullified or halved by the target; weakness and ForceField still apply

pierce_bolt.effect: as pierce_fire: Bolt (Lightning) can't be absorbed, nullified or halved by the target; weakness and ForceField still apply

parts.holder: sketch success: the sketcher; sketched-attack boosts: the SKETCHED MONSTER ($3417) as coded
parts.hook: C2/3B37 in the Sketch effect C2/3B29 (success roll); C2/2C22 in C2/2C21 (attack level $11AF); C2/4527 in C2/450D (status application masks)
parts.trigger: Sketch command on a monster; then the sketched attack's setup and its status application ($3417 = sketched monster index while it runs)
parts.effect: (1) Sketcher has Art License: the sketch always succeeds (vanilla's C2/3792 roll with Beret bonus skipped); unsketchable monsters ($3C80 bit $20) and party targets still fail. (2) If the sketched monster has Art License: attack level $11AF = max(monster level, sketcher level) (vanilla: monster level); $11AE = max(monster, sketcher) Vigor ($3B2C) for physical attacks ($11A2 bit 0) or Magic Power ($3B41) otherwise; $11A4 |= $20 (unblockable). (3) If the sketched monster has Art License: statuses the attack sets ignore target immunities ($FC/$FE = raw to-set bytes $3DD4/$3DE8 instead of AND with $331C/$3330).
parts.numbers: sketch 100%; max() of levels and of the relevant stat
parts.order: (1) replaces only the hit roll; (2) at attack-data load; (3) per target at status application
parts.vanilla_meaning: C2/3B37: roll sketch success; C2/2C21: $11AF = sketched monster's level when sketching; C2/4527: statuses masked by target vulnerability
parts.notes: (2) and (3) call jun-checker with X = $3417 (the monster), while (1) checks the sketcher - very likely a BC bug (intended holder: the sketcher). Port decision needed: as coded vs intended. Also patch_junction_elemental_pierce.txt (other group) lists art_license.

esper_attack.holder: attacker; characters only (needs an equipped esper: X < 8 and $161E,char != $FF); monsters can't (and it's on monster_banlist)
esper_attack.hook: C2/336F (damage_modification main), C2/0BD3 (pierce main), C2/0B8E (JML main-esper-attack-misc-effect, replaces LDA $11A4 / BMI at the start of C2/0B83 after the 'power = 0' exit)
esper_attack.trigger: every action of the holder (damage_modification part per strike; pierce/misc parts per target, misc only if power $11A6 != 0 and not a DoT tick)
esper_attack.effect: esper spell = equipped esper index + $36, data at C4/6AC0 + spell*14 (same 14-byte layout as $11A0-$11AD). (1) C2/336F: $11A1 |= esper spell byte 1 (elements) -> the action gains the esper's elements before element boosts/fonts/sinks. (2) C2/0BD3: those elements are removed from the resistable mask: never absorbed/nulled/halved by the target (weakness x2 applies). (3) C2/0B8E per target: $11A4 |= esper byte 4 & 3 (heal and drain flags - an esper whose spell heals makes the action heal the target, a drain one makes it drain); then 25% (jun-rng2 < $40): if the esper spell lifts status (byte 4 b2) queue removal of its statuses (bytes 10-13 -> $3DFC/$3E10), else queue infliction ($3DD4/$3DE8) minus Wound if the target is death-protected ($3AA1 b2) and minus status-4 b5 (Hide).
esper_attack.order: (1) before all element boosts; (2) before pierces; (3) before variance/defense, so the heal flag set here decides heal vs damage
esper_attack.vanilla_meaning: C2/336F Berserk; C2/0B8E: choose C2/0D87 (%HP) or C2/0C9E (normal) damage modification
esper_attack.notes: Status riders use the pending-status queues, so immunities still apply when C2/4391 processes them. Added elements also affect everything downstream (ForceField, weakness, Freeze thaw...). The 'espercutegf' flag puts EspAtk on the always list. The manifest lists patch_junction_potent_venom.txt for it, but that patch never tests EspAtk.

loner.hook: C2/336F damage_modification main (X = attacker, on $11B0 before split/crit/defense) -> main-misc
loner.trigger: every strike by the holder (damage and healing)
loner.effect: $11B0 = floor($11B0/2) x max(0, 5 - N), N = living combatants on the attacker's side (party slots for a character, monster slots for a monster), the attacker included
loner.numbers: characters: 4 alive x0.5, 3 x1, 2 x1.5, alone x2; monsters: 5-6 alive -> 0, 4 x0.5, 3 x1, 2 x1.5, alone x2; repeated addition saturating at 65535

crisis_arm.hook: C2/336F damage_modification main (X = attacker, on $11B0 before split/crit/defense) -> main-misc
crisis_arm.trigger: every strike by the holder (damage and healing)
crisis_arm.numbers: x0 .. x2.25 by the last digit of current HP (digit 0 -> nothing; average x1.125)
crisis_arm.order: step 7 (after Loner, before Gaia, Atma). full damage_modification order: see patch:patch_junction_damage_modification.txt
crisis_arm.notes: The multiplier is jun-divide's remainder (X) of curHP/10; the quotient is discarded. Fits the junction's 'luck' tag (HP last digit); if HP/10 had been intended it would be a bug, but the code is unambiguous. Uses the attacker's HP at strike time.

gaia_boost.hook: C2/336F damage_modification main (X = attacker, on $11B0 before split/crit/defense) (after main-misc)
gaia_boost.trigger: the attack's $11A1 contains the battlefield's element: dance = ED/8E5B[$11E2 battle background]; element by dance 0-7 = Wind, Pearl, Fire, Bolt, Earth, Water, Poison, Ice (Wind Song, Forest Suite, Desert Aria, Love Sonata, Earth Blues, Water Rondo, Dusk Requiem, Snowman Jazz)

atma_force.hook: C2/336F damage_modification main (X = attacker, on $11B0 before split/crit/defense) -> do-atma-force (last step)
atma_force.trigger: every strike by the holder (damage and healing)
atma_force.effect: $11B0 = 3 x floor(d x Cur / (2 x Exp)) (approx.), i.e. about x1.5 x (Cur/Exp). Characters: Cur = sum of current HP of present party members; Exp = sum over the 4 party slots of 'expected HP' = 35 + sum of the level-up HP table E6/F4A0[0..Level-2] (present member: its own level; absent slot: the attacker's). Monsters: Cur = sum of present monsters' curHP>>3, Exp = sum of their maxHP>>3 (~x1.5 x HP fraction).
atma_force.numbers: computes max(d,Cur) x (min(d,Cur)>>k) with k >= 1 chosen so the shifted value < 256, divisor Exp>>(k-1); while the 24-bit product >= 65536 halve product and divisor; 16-bit divide (divisor 0 -> 1); result x3 saturating 65535
atma_force.order: step 9, last of damage_modification. full damage_modification order: see patch:patch_junction_damage_modification.txt
atma_force.notes: Present (not living) members count: dead present members add 0 to Cur but their Exp to the divisor; absent slots add the attacker's Exp. Max HP above the base growth (HP% relics, esper bonuses) pushes the factor above 1.5. Small carry quirks (ADC without CLC) can add 1s to the sums. Port: d x 1.5 x Cur/Exp with integer flooring is a faithful approximation.

boost_crit.hook: C2/340C (JSL main, replaces INC $BC / INC $BC): critical-hit branch of the strike routine
boost_crit.trigger: the strike is a critical (vanilla 1/32 roll at C2/3400 or any other path to C2/340C)
boost_crit.effect: vanilla $BC += 2 kept; if the attacker has Crit Boost, $11B0 x1.5 (rounded up) before the $BC multiplier
boost_crit.numbers: d' = d + floor(d/2) + (d & 1) (LSR then ADC without CLC), saturating 65535; then vanilla crit x2 via $BC -> about x3 total
boost_crit.order: after damage_modification and hit determination; before C2/341C (x(1+$BC/2)), per-target variance/defense/elements

faith.hook: C2/22A8 (JML main, replaces BIT #$40 / BNE $22EC) in hit determination C2/220D, after 'can't dodge -> hit' (C2/22A1)
faith.trigger: non-physical action ($11A2 b0 clear) without the level-based-hit flag ($11A4 b6)
faith.effect: if attacker or target has Faith: auto-hit (jump to C2/22E8), skipping stamina evade ($11A4 b4) and the hit-rate/MBlock roll (C2/22FB...)
faith.order: after Clear handling, Reflect/Repel, death-protection miss ($11A2 b1), only-dead mismatch and Interceptor; status immunities and later effects still apply
faith.vanilla_meaning: C2/22A8: level-based hit (L.x spells) -> C2/22EC; else stamina/hit-rate rolls
faith.notes: Side effect: physical actions now skip the level-based test (they jump to C2/22AC); vanilla physical attacks don't use b6. A target with Faith is hit by every spell that reaches the roll.

heal_boost.hook: C2/62F7 damage_trigger main (per combatant Y with pending $33D0/$33E4, X = attacker, before C2/12F5 applies it) -> check-heal
heal_boost.trigger: per combatant Y with pending healing ($33E4,Y != $FFFF) from the action
heal_boost.numbers: h + floor(h/2), saturating $FFFE; capped 9999 at the end of main
heal_boost.order: first in main for Y: Heal Boost -> Heal Font -> Heal Sink -> Blood Mage block; later Double Time x0.5 and Chemist x2 also hit healing. full damage_trigger order: see patch:patch_junction_damage_trigger.txt
heal_boost.notes: Covers every kind of healing the holder's action produces: heal spells/items, regen ticks (attacker = self), drain and elemental-absorb healing, Distribute shares, MP healing.

heal_font.hook: C2/62F7 damage_trigger main (per combatant Y with pending $33D0/$33E4, X = attacker, before C2/12F5 applies it) -> check-heal
heal_font.trigger: per combatant Y with pending healing, from any healer
heal_font.effect: healing x1.25 per living Heal Font holder
heal_font.order: after Heal Boost, before Heal Sink
heal_font.notes: 'living' = jun-check-entity-living: character bit in $3A74 and not Wound ($3EE4 b7) and not Hidden ($3EF9 b5); monster bit in $3A75. Count covers all 10 slots, both sides (attacker, targets, bystanders); each holder's check is a separate jun-checker call (each can be cancelled by Junction Jammer).

heal_sink.effect: healing x0.75 per living Heal Sink holder
heal_sink.notes: 'living' = jun-check-entity-living: character bit in $3A74 and not Wound ($3EE4 b7) and not Hidden ($3EF9 b5); monster bit in $3A75. Count covers all 10 slots, both sides (attacker, targets, bystanders); each holder's check is a separate jun-checker call (each can be cancelled by Junction Jammer).

blood_mage.hook: C2/62F7 damage_trigger main (per combatant Y with pending $33D0/$33E4, X = attacker, before C2/12F5 applies it) -> do-blood-restriction (this group's part only)
blood_mage.trigger: Y == attacker (self), the action has an MP cost ($11A5 != 0) and is a heal ($11A4 b0), and the caster has Blood Mage
blood_mage.effect: the caster's own pending healing from that spell is set to 0 (displayed as 0)
blood_mage.notes: Main Blood Mage effect is in the gold_blood_mage/prehit patches (other group). Here: a Blood Mage can't heal itself with MP-cost healing spells (allies still healed).

parts.hook: C2/5D39 battle-menu HP/MP copy (C2/5D26); C2/32B6 end-of-action MP deduction; C2/3F47 MP-critical weapon effect; C2/4973 end-of-battle MP save
parts.trigger: whenever the holder's MP is read for display (menu refresh), and whenever it pays MP
parts.effect: MP is derived from HP: current MP = floor(HP/8), max MP shown/stored = 999 ($3C08/$3C30 and the menu copies). Paying cost c (spells at C2/32B6, if c != 0): MP check uses current MP vs c; enough -> HP -= 8*c (no floor; HP can reach exactly 0 without Wound) and MP is left = c until the next refresh; not enough -> vanilla 'not enough MP' fail. MP-critical weapons (random 0-7 + base): HP -= 8*that as well. End of battle: battle MP is not written back to the character record. prehit flags attacker and target for spell-list refresh ($3204 bit7) every hit determination.
parts.numbers: MP = HP/8; cost x8 in HP
parts.order: blood_mage wins over gold_mage at C2/32B6 and in the menu; at C2/3F47 both deduct if both present
parts.vanilla_meaning: C2/32B6: MP -= queued cost; C2/5D39: copy MP to menu; C2/4973: save MP
parts.notes: The refresh in cast-check writes $3C08,Y where Y may not be the caster (Y not set at C2/32B6); the check then uses $3C08,X as last refreshed. Port: MP := HP/8 before checking. mp_switch is disabled for holders.

brace.hook: C2/62F7 damage_trigger main (per combatant Y with pending $33D0/$33E4, X = attacker, before C2/12F5 applies it) -> check-brace
brace.trigger: Y is Defending ($3AA1,Y b1) and has pending damage of any kind
brace.order: after the heal steps, before Catch/Double Time/Chemist. full damage_trigger order: see patch:patch_junction_damage_trigger.txt
brace.notes: Vanilla Defend only halves physical damage (C2/0D02); Brace halves everything, so physical damage while defending is about 1/4.

catch.hook: C2/62F7 damage_trigger main (per combatant Y with pending $33D0/$33E4, X = attacker, before C2/12F5 applies it) -> check-catch
catch.trigger: command $B5 = $08 (Throw) and Y has pending damage or healing
catch.effect: Y's pending damage set to 0. If Y is a party member and $3A7A is still $08: 50% (jun-rng1 carry clear) Y gets one of the thrown item: $3401 = $B0 (battle message 'Got <item> 1 !'), $2F35 = $32F4,Y = $B6 (item id), Y's bit set in $3A8C (vanilla 'add reserved item to inventory').
catch.order: after Brace, before Double Time. full damage_trigger order: see patch:patch_junction_damage_trigger.txt
catch.notes: Monsters with Catch only nullify Throw damage. The thrower's item is still used up. If a Meatbone/Auto-Potion trigger earlier in the same loop changed $3A7A, no item is gained.

double_time.hook: C2/01BE (JSL main + 4 NOP, replaces INC $3219,X / BNE / DEC $3219,X) in end-of-turn handling; and C2/62F7 damage_trigger main (per combatant Y with pending $33D0/$33E4, X = attacker, before C2/12F5 applies it)
double_time.trigger: (a) the holder's turn ends with its action queue finished (vanilla path C2/01B7, not when $3AA0 b3 'ATB stopped'); (b) every pending damage/healing its actions produce
double_time.effect: (a) ATB gauge top byte $3219,X set to $80 (gauge restarts half full) instead of vanilla's saturating +1 (restart from ~empty); if it was $FF it stays $FF. (b) all damage and healing dealt by the holder x0.5.
double_time.order: (b) after Heal Boost/Font/Sink and Brace/Catch, before Chemist. full damage_trigger order: see patch:patch_junction_damage_trigger.txt
double_time.vanilla_meaning: C2/01BE: after a turn, INC the ATB top byte (saturating at $FF)
double_time.notes: Net: about twice as many turns at half effect. Halving also applies to its heals, drains and MP damage.

chemist.hook: C2/62F7 damage_trigger main (per combatant Y with pending $33D0/$33E4, X = attacker, before C2/12F5 applies it)
chemist.effect: all pending healing and damage from that action x2
chemist.order: after Double Time, before Reverse. full damage_trigger order: see patch:patch_junction_damage_trigger.txt
chemist.notes: Includes an Auto-Potion queued Potion (command 1) if its user has Chemist. Not Throw ($08) or Tools ($09).

reverse.hook: C2/62F7 damage_trigger main (per combatant Y with pending $33D0/$33E4, X = attacker, before C2/12F5 applies it) -> reverse-damage
reverse.trigger: per Y with pending damage or healing from the holder's action, unless the action's $3A7C = $22 (periodic status tick)
reverse.effect: swap Y's pending damage ($33D0) and healing ($33E4): damage heals, healing damages (incl. the $FFFF 'none' markers and the attacker's own drain healing)
reverse.order: after Chemist, before Precision (Precision then removes converted damage on the holder's own side). full damage_trigger order: see patch:patch_junction_damage_trigger.txt
reverse.notes: Never on monsters (monster_banlist + every_monster blacklist). MP actions swap MP damage/healing the same way. Statuses unaffected.

precision.hook: C2/62F7 damage_trigger main (per combatant Y with pending $33D0/$33E4, X = attacker, before C2/12F5 applies it) -> check-precision
precision.trigger: per Y with pending damage: the action's target set ($B8/$B9) has >= 2 bits, and Y is on the attacker's side (both < 8 or both >= 8; includes the attacker itself)
precision.effect: Y's pending damage set to $FFFF (no damage); healing untouched
precision.order: after Reverse, before Meatbone/Auto-Potion/Corrosive/Juggler. full damage_trigger order: see patch:patch_junction_damage_trigger.txt
precision.notes: Multi-target attacks never hurt the holder's allies (e.g. Quake/Merton). $B8 can be clobbered by a Meatbone/Auto-Potion trigger earlier in the same loop (sets one target), which turns Precision off for the remaining lower-index combatants.

meatbone_cut.hook: C2/62F7 damage_trigger main (per combatant Y with pending $33D0/$33E4, X = attacker, before C2/12F5 applies it) -> do-meatbone-auto-potion
meatbone_cut.trigger: per Y with pending HP damage, before it's applied: counters allowed ($341A != 0); not MP damage ($11A3 b7); not a DoT tick; damage non-zero, not $FFFF and < Y's current HP (non-lethal, after the earlier modifiers); attacker != Y; Y's current (pre-hit) HP <= floor(maxHP/8)
meatbone_cut.effect: Y queues a counter (C2/4EB2): command $44 (BC's custom 'final attack' command, patch_junction_command_final_attack) with spell $92 Revenge, aimed at the combatant in $32E0,Y (who last attacked Y, normally this attacker), only if that combatant is alive
meatbone_cut.numbers: threshold: pre-hit curHP <= maxHP>>3; Revenge damage = Y's maxHP - curHP when it resolves
meatbone_cut.order: after Precision; before Auto-Potion, Corrosive, Juggler, cap. full damage_trigger order: see patch:patch_junction_damage_trigger.txt
meatbone_cut.notes: Writes $B8/$B9 and $3A7A/$3A7B ($44/$92). Uses pre-hit HP: a hit that drops you from above 1/8 to below does not trigger; you must already be at <= 1/8. Can fire together with Auto-Potion on the same hit. 'DoT tick' = jun-check-is-damage-over-time: self-targeted action (attacker == Y) with $3A7C = $22 and $B5 = $12, i.e. the periodic Poison/Regen/Seizure-type status tick.

auto_potion.hook: C2/62F7 damage_trigger main (per combatant Y with pending $33D0/$33E4, X = attacker, before C2/12F5 applies it) -> do-meatbone-auto-potion
auto_potion.trigger: same gate as Meatbone Cut (counters allowed, HP damage, non-zero, non-lethal, not DoT) but no HP threshold and attacker may be Y; skipped if $3A7A = $01 and $B1 b0 (the current action is itself a reaction Item - loop guard)
auto_potion.effect: party member: needs a Potion ($E9) in inventory; one is removed now and $32F4,Y = $E9 (returned if the action is cancelled). Monster: 50% (jun-rng1), no item used. Then Y queues command $01 Item, item $E9 (Potion) on itself; all allies ($B8=$0F / $B9=$3F) if Y also has Salve
auto_potion.numbers: monster 50%; party: one Potion per trigger
auto_potion.order: after Meatbone; before Corrosive, Juggler, cap. full damage_trigger order: see patch:patch_junction_damage_trigger.txt
auto_potion.notes: Triggers per damaging strike (multi-hit attacks can drink several). Potion amount from vanilla item data; Heal Boost/Chemist of Y apply when it resolves.

salve.hook: C2/62F7 damage_trigger main (per combatant Y with pending $33D0/$33E4, X = attacker, before C2/12F5 applies it) -> retarget-salve (this group's part only)
salve.trigger: Auto-Potion triggers for a holder of both Auto-Potion and Salve
salve.effect: the queued Potion targets all allies instead of self (jun-set-target-allies: $B8 = $0F or $B9 = $3F)
salve.notes: Main Salve effect is in patch_junction_taunt_salve.txt (other group).

parts.holder: attacker (the item user); in the menu, the character whose menu is open ($7E62CA)
parts.hook: menu C1/8925 (JSL salve-target-group replaces LDA $2688,X / STA $7A84: item's targeting byte for the cursor); battle C2/58ED main-target-manipulation (after Taunt/Camouflage)
parts.trigger: menu: choosing an item whose item-data type (D8/5000 byte0 & 7) is 6 ('Item' class: Tonic..Megalixir, Phoenix Down, Echo Screen, skeans etc.) and whose targeting byte lacks $40 (doesn't default to enemies). Battle: Item command ($B5 = $01) whose target set reaches the single-target collapse at C2/58ED.
parts.effect: menu: cursor targeting byte |= $28 (group-of-one-side by default + toggle single/multi), so the item can be aimed at the whole party (or a whole side). Battle: if the user has Salve, C2/58ED returns to C2/58F4 (STA $B8 without JSR $522A) so ALL chosen targets are kept instead of one random one. One item is consumed as usual.
parts.numbers: none; vanilla multi-target halving (C2/3385: $3EC9 >= 2 and $11A2 bit $40 clear -> $11B0 / 2) still applies; items load $11A2 = $21 (no 'no-split' bit), so a Salve'd item hitting 2+ targets very likely has its computed amount halved (not verified for fixed/percentage item effects)
parts.order: battle: after Taunt and Camouflage (both no-ops when using items on one's own party), replaces the vanilla random pick
parts.vanilla_meaning: C1/8925: STA item targeting byte for the menu cursor; C2/58ED: collapse a single-target attack's mask to one random target
parts.notes: Battle-side 'is consumable' check is buggy: salve-check-item-is-consumable does TAX with 8-bit X (X is 8-bit inside C2/587E), so it reads D8/5000+((item*30)&$FF) and returns 'not type 6' for all 29 type-6 items; combined with the inverted branch (BEQ just-return on 'consumable') the net effect is: every Item-command use by a Salve holder keeps all its targets. Menu side uses 16-bit X and works as intended. Items that default to enemies (throwing skeans) are not widened in the menu. For the port: holder's healing/support items (type 6, non-enemy-default) may target a whole side; apply each target, consume one.

corrosive.hook: C2/62F7 damage_trigger main (per combatant Y with pending $33D0/$33E4, X = attacker, before C2/12F5 applies it) -> do-corrosive
corrosive.trigger: per Y with pending damage < $4000 from the holder's action, not a DoT tick
corrosive.effect: HP action: Y's max HP -= (min(d, Y current HP) + 2) >> 2. MP action ($11A3 b7): Y's max MP -= (min(d, Y current MP) + 2) >> 2.
corrosive.numbers: about 25% of the damage actually dealt (rounded), lowering battle max HP/MP permanently for the battle
corrosive.order: after Meatbone/Auto-Potion, before Juggler and the 9999 cap (so a boosted d >= $4000 skips it). full damage_trigger order: see patch:patch_junction_damage_trigger.txt
corrosive.notes: Uses pre-damage current HP for the min. Current HP is not clamped to the new max. Hits allies/self too if the holder damages them. No floor on max HP (an overhealed target taking big hits could underflow it in theory).

juggler.hook: C2/62F7 damage_trigger main (per combatant Y with pending $33D0/$33E4, X = attacker, before C2/12F5 applies it) -> do-juggler
juggler.trigger: per Y with pending damage or healing from an action, not a DoT tick
juggler.effect: physical action: make Defense >= Magic Defense (swap $3BB8/$3BB9) and Evade better than MBlock (stored $3B54 <= $3B55, lower = better; swap otherwise). Non-physical: the reverse (MDef >= Def, MBlock better than Evade). Swaps persist for the battle.
juggler.order: last junction step before the cap; this hit's damage is already computed, so it only helps against later hits. full damage_trigger order: see patch:patch_junction_damage_trigger.txt
juggler.notes: Also triggers on being healed (non-physical branch). Stored evade/mblock are the vanilla transformed bytes (256-2*value style).

damage_split.hook: C2/62F1 (JSL main-calc, replaces STZ $F0 / STZ $F2) -> check-calc, once per strike for Y = $12..0 before the main loop
damage_split.trigger: Y has non-zero, non-$FFFF pending damage < Y's current HP (non-lethal)
damage_split.effect: q = floor(d/4) is moved to the attacker: attacker's pending damage += q ($FFFF counts as 0); Y's damage = d - q
damage_split.order: before Distribute (same Y) and before every main-loop modifier (Brace, Double Time... then act on the reduced/added amounts); the attacker's new total is capped 9999 by main
damage_split.notes: No split if the hit would be lethal. MP actions split as MP (threshold still compares with HP). If Y is the attacker itself the math is odd (adds then re-splits).

distribute.hook: C2/62F1 main-calc -> check-calc (before the main loop)
distribute.trigger: Y has pending healing h and h + curHP >= maxHP
distribute.effect: Y's healing = maxHP - curHP; overflow = h + curHP - maxHP split evenly (integer division) among the other living members of Y's side (party slots for characters, monster slots for monsters); each gets + share to its pending healing ($FFFF counts as 0). No other living ally -> overflow lost.
distribute.order: after Damage Split for the same Y; before Heal Boost/Font/Sink (which then scale the trimmed amount and the shares)
distribute.notes: Bug: if Y is above max HP (Overheal), maxHP - curHP underflows to a huge heal that main caps at 9999.

nihopalaoa.hook: C2/2AF2 (JSL main-nihopalaoa, re-executes LDA $D85000,X) in the item attack-data loader C2/2A37, after the item's flags/statuses are copied to $11A2/$11A4/$11AA
nihopalaoa.effect: $11A4 &= ~$05 (heal -> damage, lift status -> inflict status); $11A2 &= ~$04 ('only hits dead' cleared, so revive items hit the living); then if the item inflicts Wound ($11AA b7) or is %HP ($11A4 b7), set $11A2 b1 (miss vs death-protected targets)
nihopalaoa.vanilla_meaning: C2/2AF2: item type; special handler for type-0 items
nihopalaoa.notes: Potions/Elixirs damage, Remedy-type items inflict their statuses, Phoenix Down kills unless the target is death-protected. Throw ($08) and Tools are not affected.

overheal.holder: attacker (the healer; X saved by C2/12F5)
overheal.hook: C2/132A (JSL main; rest of the old code BRA'd over) in C2/1323 HP-heal application; C2/41EC (JSL main-revenge) in special effect C2/41E6 (Revenge); C1/1B6B display (see patch:patch_over_9999_maxhp.txt)
overheal.trigger: net HP healing (C2/13A7) would bring HP to >= max HP
overheal.effect: base = max(curHP, maxHP); excess = min(curHP + heal - base, maxHP); new HP = base + ((excess + 2) >> 2), saturating 65535; never lower than current.
overheal.numbers: 25% of the overflow (rounded), at most about +maxHP/4 per heal; no hard cap besides 65535; per-action heal already capped 9999
overheal.order: HP application stage, after all damage_trigger modifiers
overheal.vanilla_meaning: C2/132A: HP += heal, capped at max HP
overheal.notes: Always-on: for non-holders a heal past max sets HP = max(maxHP, curHP), i.e. healing no longer pulls an overhealed HP back down (vanilla set it to max). Revenge (C2/41E6, $11B0 = maxHP - curHP): if curHP > maxHP it now heals by curHP - maxHP (sets $11A4 b0) instead of a huge wrap-around. MP untouched. Not checked: what happens to HP > max after battle (vanilla copies battle HP back). Interacts badly with Distribute (see distribute).

potent_venom.hook: C2/4456 (JML main + 2 NOP, re-executes ORA/STA $3E10,Y) in status application C2/4406, per target; exits to C2/445C (vanilla 'miss if nothing changes') or C2/447D (skip it)
potent_venom.trigger: the action would inflict Poison ($FC b2: $11AA has Poison, target not already Poisoned); for special effect $11A9 = $42 (BC labels it Rippler; $11A9 holds effect*2) the attacker must itself be Poisoned; the target is immune to Poison ($331C,Y b2 clear)
potent_venom.effect: 50% (jun-rng1): if the attacker has Potent Venom, Poison is written straight into the target's status ($3EE4,Y |= $04), bypassing immunity and the status queue, and the miss check is skipped
potent_venom.order: after hit determination, before special effect C2/387E and damage C2/0B83; non-immune targets get Poison the vanilla way
potent_venom.vanilla_meaning: C2/4456: queue statuses-to-clear 3-4 ($3E10); then if $11A7 b0 and nothing changeable -> target missed
potent_venom.notes: Always-on: if the target is already Poisoned and the action is the periodic tick ($3A7C = $22), the miss check is skipped (so ticks on force-poisoned immune targets aren't flagged as misses). Direct write skips Poison's on-set handling. The manifest also lists this patch for esper_attack, but it never tests EspAtk.

barehanded.hook: C2/28EA (JSL main + NOP, replaces LDA $AC / STA $3B68,X) in the battle stat loader (D = $1100, so $AC/$AD = $11AC/$11AD, the hands' battle power)
barehanded.trigger: the character's stats are loaded (battle start) and both hands are empty ($161F/$1620 = $FF)
barehanded.effect: both hands' battle power ($3B68,X and $3B69,X) = min(255, 5 x Level + $11AC + 256 x $11AD)
barehanded.notes: Vanilla bare-hand values: both start as the character's base Battle Power (ED/7CAA, C2/0EA2) and C2/0F64/C2/0F6B zero a hand in some hand configurations. Normally the left value is 0 for empty hands, giving min(255, 5 x Level + base BP); if the left value is non-zero the 16-bit sum is >= 256 and BP becomes 255. Holding any weapon/shield in a hand slot: vanilla behaviour.

time_font.hook: C2/09E4 (JSL main, replaces TYA / STA $3ADD,X) in C2/09D2 (per-combatant timer/ATB multiplier set-up); C2/24C1 (JSL main-initialize) at battle init
time_font.trigger: whenever C2/09D2 runs for a combatant: battle start (main-initialize sets $3204 b2 for all 10 slots and runs C2/083F), after each of that combatant's turns (vanilla sets $3204 b2 at C2/0190) and other vanilla recomputes
time_font.effect: n = (#living Time Font) - (#living Time Sink); $3ADD,X (status-timer speed: 32 Slow / 64 normal / 84 Haste) x1.25 per net font or x0.75 per net sink, cap 255. $3ADD drives only the status clock C2/5A83 ($3ADC += $3ADD; each overflow advances Stop, Condemned/Doom, Sleep/Freeze-type countdowns and the Poison/Regen/Seizure-type periodic ticks). The ATB fill increment $3AC8 is computed from the unmodified Y and is NOT changed.
time_font.numbers: v = m x 32; per net font v += floor(v/4); per net sink v = floor(v/2) + floor(v/4); $3ADD = min(255, floor(v/32)). Normal: +1 -> 80, +2 -> 100, -1 -> 48, -2 -> 36; Haste +1 -> 105
time_font.order: replaces the $3ADD store only; ATB speed path untouched
time_font.vanilla_meaning: C2/09E4: $3ADD,X = 32/64/84 by Slow/Haste (then C2/09E8 computes $3AC8 from Y and speed)
time_font.notes: Global and symmetric: changes every combatant's status timers, both sides. Despite the name/tags (haste) it does not speed ATB (likely BC treated $3ADD as 'the ATB multiplier' as many docs call it). A combatant's value refreshes only when its multiplier is recalculated (start, after its turns, Haste/Slow).

time_sink.effect: as time_font with the sign reversed: each net Time Sink multiplies every combatant's status-timer speed $3ADD by 0.75
time_sink.notes: Font and Sink cancel by count (n = fonts - sinks), unlike element fonts/sinks.

luck_font.hook: core jun-rng2 (61/0A40), reached from vanilla RNG via patch_junction_luck_font_sink.txt
luck_font.effect: No effect in CE 6.1.3: jun-rng2 is just JSL jun-rng2-noluck; the luck code is commented out (# lines in the raw core). It is also on always_banlist, which randomize() adds to every category's banlist, so it is never assigned. Intended (commented) algorithm: n = #living Luck Font - #living Luck Sink; n > 0: roll r; n times: 50% re-roll and keep the lower; n < 0: |n| times 50% re-roll and keep the higher - applied to every battle RNG call (lower = luckier for crits/hits).
luck_font.notes: Port: implement as no-op (or skip). See patch:patch_junction_luck_font_sink.txt.

luck_sink.effect: No effect in CE 6.1.3 (commented out, always banned); see luck_font for the intended opposite (keep higher rolls).

critical_haste.holder: self (the combatant that enters Near Fatal; party or monster)
critical_haste.hook: C2/0A5D (JML main) inside vanilla C2/0A4A, the low-HP relic routine called for every present combatant from the battle-state update C2/083F; plus C2/5BFF (battle-timer increment) which forces one extra C2/083F run when the global battle timer $3A44 first becomes 1
critical_haste.trigger: SOS TRIGGER (same for every critical_* key): during the state update (C2/083F runs after every action via C2/141D, and once more when $3A44 ticks 0->1), for combatant X with $3AA0 bit0 (present), $3AA0 bit4 clear, Near Fatal status ($3EE5 bit1; vanilla sets it at about 1/8 of max HP - use the game's own Near Fatal/critical state) and $3205 bit1 still set. $3205 is filled with $FF at battle start (C2/23FD fill of $2A10-$341F) and nothing but this routine clears bit1, so it fires ONCE PER BATTLE per combatant slot (first time the holder is in Near Fatal at a state update), not per hit. If $B1 bit7 is set (vanilla busy flag, set C2/4918 / cleared C2/015A) or $3A44 is still 0, the routine exits WITHOUT clearing the flag, i.e. it is postponed, not lost. On firing it clears $3205 bit1 (as vanilla).
critical_haste.effect: auto-casts spell $1F Haste on itself: jun-queue-self-spell = vanilla C2/4E91 with command $26 (the Barrier-Ring/Mithril-Glove auto-cast). Goes into the global special-action queue ($340A). Command $26 handler C2/4F5F: spell = queued $B8, $B5 = $02 (Magic animation), $11A3 := $02 (unreflectable; all other flags2 bits cleared), $11A4 |= $20 (can't be dodged), $11A5 := 0 (no MP), then C2/3167 forces the target to the caster only ($B8 = own bit). So every SOS spell hits only the holder. The special queue runs first in the main loop (before counters and normal turns) with $B1 bit0 set, so vanilla counters and return_magic ignore it.
critical_haste.order: inside the SOS routine: all SOS spells in index order 0x20..0x2D (Haste, Bserk, Float, Vanish, Warp, Quick, Cure3, Remedy, Regen, Life3, Golem, Fenrir, Rabbit, Freeze), then SOS commands 0x30..0x34, then Morph, Dance, Escape; then the vanilla low-HP relic casts (Shell $25 / Safe $1C / Reflect $24 from $3C59) run as before. Several SOS junctions on one holder all fire.
critical_haste.vanilla_meaning: C2/0A4A: if Near Fatal and the once-per-battle $3205 bit1 is set, clear it and auto-cast the low-HP relic spells (Barrier Ring, Mithril Glove, ...) on self via command $26
critical_haste.notes: Port: per combatant, a 'SOS used' flag reset at battle start; check after every action and once right after the battle clock starts; queue a free, self-only, unreflectable, undodgeable cast. Monsters can hold SOS junctions too.

critical_bserk.trigger: SOS trigger (see critical_haste: first Near Fatal of the battle, at a state update)
critical_bserk.effect: auto-casts spell $21 Bserk on itself via command $26 (self only, MP 0, unreflectable, undodgeable)
critical_bserk.order: 2nd in the SOS spell loop (see critical_haste)
critical_bserk.notes: Berserk makes the holder uncontrollable (Fight only) for the rest of the status.

critical_float.effect: auto-casts spell $22 Float on itself via command $26 (self only, MP 0, unreflectable, undodgeable)

critical_vanish.effect: auto-casts spell $26 Vanish (Clear status) on itself via command $26 (self only, MP 0, unreflectable, undodgeable). BC comment: command $26 is used so several SOS spells can proc without the later ones undoing Vanish (they are not 'magic hits' that remove Clear).

critical_warp.effect: auto-casts spell $2A Warp on itself via command $26 (special effect $18 = vanilla Warp escape)
critical_warp.notes: Unlike SOS Escape, BC does not check the can't-run flags ($B1 & $06) here; whether Warp works is left to the vanilla Warp effect (which refuses in no-escape battles). For a monster holder the vanilla Warp effect's result is unverified.

critical_quick.hook: C2/0A5D in C2/0A4A (see critical_haste); C2/11BB ATB add (patch_instant_enemy_quick)
critical_quick.effect: auto-casts spell $2B Quick on itself via command $26 (vanilla Quick: $3404 = holder, other combatants' timers frozen for its extra turns). patch_instant_enemy_quick (global, not junction-gated): every ATB tick, if X == $3404 (current Quick holder) its ATB high byte $3219,X is set to $FF before the add, so it is full at once and acts immediately each Quick turn.
critical_quick.vanilla_meaning: C2/11BB: ATB += $3AC8,X; vanilla Quick still waits for the holder's ATB to fill
critical_quick.notes: The instant-ATB change applies to every Quick (spell, item, any combatant), mainly so monsters under Quick act at once.

critical_cure3.effect: auto-casts spell $2F Cure 3 on itself only via command $26 (normally party-wide; forced single self target, so no split)

critical_remedy.effect: auto-casts spell $33 Remedy on itself via command $26

critical_regen.effect: auto-casts spell $34 Regen on itself via command $26

critical_life3.effect: auto-casts spell $35 Life 3 (Reraise status) on itself via command $26

critical_golem.effect: auto-casts spell $4C Golem (esper) via command $26, target forced to self; Golem's guard effect (special $11) is the vanilla one (it guards based on the caster), not limited by the self target
critical_golem.notes: Animation is the Magic-command path with the esper spell id; whether the full summon animation plays is vanilla behaviour of command $26 with an esper spell (unverified).

critical_fenrir.effect: auto-casts spell $4E Fenrir (Image status) on itself only via command $26

critical_rabbit.effect: auto-casts spell $FE Lagomorph (healing, power 10, normally party-wide) on itself only via command $26

critical_freeze.effect: auto-casts spell $CF Cold Dust (ice element, power 0, inflicts Freeze) on itself via command $26: the holder freezes itself
critical_freeze.notes: Meant to combine with null_freeze (frozen holder can't be hit) and allies' firestarter. Freeze being set also fires the firestarter hook (C2/4692).

critical_runic.effect: queues command $0B Runic for the holder: jun-queue-command (C2/4EB2 = the holder's counterattack queue $32CD / list $3920, runs right after the current action), $3A7A = $0B, $3A7B = 0, targets $B8/$B9 = 0, queued MP cost 0. Holder takes the vanilla Runic stance. (Counter queue: runs before normal turns; see patch:patch_junction_command_expansion.txt for queue semantics.)
critical_runic.order: first of the SOS command loop (0x30..0x34), after all SOS spells

critical_gprain.effect: queues command $18 GP Rain (counter queue, $3A7B = 0, targets 0) - vanilla GP Rain (spends party gold) with no preset target, so the command's own default targeting applies
critical_gprain.notes: Target selection with $B8/$B9 = 0 is left to vanilla retargeting (unverified which enemies get hit). A monster holder would run the vanilla GP Rain handler too.

critical_esper.effect: queues new command $40 (junction Summon, see patch:patch_junction_command_summon.txt) in the counter queue: a character summons its equipped esper (spell = esper + $36) for free; no esper equipped = nothing; a monster summons a random esper 0..26 uniformly

critical_jump.effect: queues new command $41 (see patch:patch_junction_command_jump.txt) in the counter queue; when it runs it puts a vanilla Jump (command $16) in the holder's normal action queue aimed at whoever last hit the holder ($32E0), so the holder leaps off-screen (untargetable) and lands later

critical_defend.effect: queues command $15 Defend for the holder (counter queue, $3A7B = 0, targets 0): vanilla defend stance

critical_dance.effect: picks the battle background's dance (table ED/8E5B indexed by background $11E2), stores it as current dance in $32E1,Y, calls vanilla pick-dance-move C2/059C (random step of that dance: slot0 7/16, slot1 6/16, slot2 2/16, slot3 1/16) into $3A7B, and queues command $13 Dance for the holder (counter queue). The holder dances (vanilla Dance command, which also sets Dance status = keeps auto-dancing).
critical_dance.notes: BUG?: the dance is written to $32E1,Y but the holder is X; Y is whatever C2/083F left (no TXY on the main path), so the holder's own $32E1 may be unset and the vanilla Dance handler then uses $3A6F / its own logic. Port: set the holder's current dance to the background dance. The queued targets $B8/$B9 are leftovers (0 if an SOS command was queued just before).

critical_morph.trigger: SOS trigger (see critical_haste), and the party Morph supply $1CF6 >= $10
critical_morph.effect: queues command $03 Morph for the holder (counter queue); $3A7B and $B8/$B9 are not set (leftovers). Vanilla Morph then transforms the holder (uses the shared morph supply).
critical_morph.order: after the SOS command loop, before Dance and Escape
critical_morph.notes: Any character (not only Terra) and even monsters can be queued Morph; behaviour for non-Terra / monster actors is whatever the vanilla Morph handler does (unverified).

critical_escape.trigger: SOS trigger (see critical_haste), and the battle allows escape: ($B1 & $06) == 0 (bit1 can't-run, bit2 can't-escape, set from monster flags)
critical_escape.effect: auto-casts spell $C2 Escape on itself via command $26 (vanilla monster-flee spell: special effect $27, sets Hide) - the holder leaves the battle
critical_escape.order: last thing queued by the SOS routine
critical_escape.notes: For a character holder the vanilla Escape effect on a party member is unverified (intended: that character runs away).

add_steal.hook: C2/31B6 (JSL main) in the per-strike attack executor C2/317B, right after JSR $37EB (weapon spell-proc conversion); plus C2/39A1 (JML main-steal) at the start of the vanilla steal effect C2/399E
add_steal.trigger: every strike of any action (not damage-over-time ticks: skipped when actor==target, $3A7C == $22 and $B5 == $12) whose special effect $11A9 == 0; 50% (jun-rng1); attacker has add_steal
add_steal.effect: $11A9 := $A4 (the Steal/Mug special effect, as vanilla Capture sets at C2/31AE) so every target hit by the strike gets a steal attempt with the vanilla steal formula. main-steal (applies to ALL steals, not only add_steal): no steal if attacker and target are on the same team (silent exit); monsters steal GP as vanilla; a character that already stole an item this action ($32F4,X != $FF) gets no further steal and no message; otherwise $3401 = 1 and vanilla continues.
add_steal.numbers: 50% per strike; only attacks without another special effect
add_steal.vanilla_meaning: C2/31B6: clear $B2 bit5 and continue strike setup; C2/39A1: Steal routine sets message 1 and branches monster vs character
add_steal.notes: Works with magic too (any command). One successful item steal per character per action.

vorpal.hook: C2/31B6 in the per-strike executor C2/317B (see add_steal)
vorpal.trigger: every physical strike ($11A2 bit0) by the holder, not DoT ticks

gunblade.hook: C2/31B6 in the per-strike executor C2/317B (see add_steal)
gunblade.trigger: every physical strike with command Fight ($B5 == 0) by the holder, if a Super Ball (item $FA) can be consumed: party holder = 1 from inventory, monster holder = from one of its steal slots (slot set to $FF)
gunblade.effect: the strike: $B3 &= ~$92 (ignore Clear, ALWAYS CRITICAL, bit4 cleared), $B3 |= $20 (ignore row), $11A4 |= $20 (can't be dodged); plus a follow-up via the vanilla weapon spell-proc mechanism: $3400 = $D1 HyperDrive, $B2 &= ~$10, $3A70 += 1, so one extra strike casts HyperDrive (power 118, ignores defense, non-elemental, MP 0) at the same target
gunblade.numbers: 1 Super Ball per Fight strike; HyperDrive $D1
gunblade.order: after vorpal; each Fight strike (Genji/Offering) consumes another ball
gunblade.notes: If the same strike also gets an esper_magic proc (C2/3250, end of strike) $3400 is overwritten by the esper spell and $3A70 is bumped twice (HyperDrive lost, one extra plain strike). $B3 bit4 meaning unverified.

quickening.hook: C2/31B6 in the per-strike executor C2/317B; C2/1771 (null-secondary-data) in the Magic/Lore/Summon path C2/175F
quickening.trigger: a strike whose spell-data MP cost $11A5 != 0 AND whose queued MP cost $3A4C != 0 (so Magic/Lore/X-Magic/Summon/monster spells), $B7 == $FF (not suppressed), caster can act (living, not Zombie/Petrify/Wound/Berserk/Muddled/Sleep/Stop/Freeze), current HP != 0, has quickening, and at least one target ($B8/$B9) alive; not DoT ticks. The new cost c' = max(ceil(1.5 * $3A4C), $11A5); requires current MP >= c' (checked before this cast's own MP is deducted).
quickening.effect: queues two counter-queue actions for the caster: (1) command $45 fixed damage: c' HP damage to itself; (2) command $42 custom-MP spell: recast the same spell ($B6) at the same targets, its MP cost $3A4C := c'. The echo runs the same strike code, so it can trigger Quickening again: a chain c, 1.5c, 2.25c, ... until MP < next cost. If ceil(1.5*$3A4C) > 255: do-quickening-penalty first (this battle: max HP, HP, max MP, MP and level each set to h + h/2 with h = (v+1)>>1, about 3/4) and c' = 255.
quickening.numbers: cost x1.5 rounded up (LSR then ADC with carry), min = spell's base cost, cap 255 with the 3/4 stat penalty; HP cost = MP cost
quickening.order: after gunblade, before astral/vampire. Fixed-damage self hit is queued first, echo second.
quickening.vanilla_meaning: per-strike attack setup; C2/1771: Slot zeroes MP cost
quickening.notes: $B7 carries the echo cost to command $42 (not stored in the queue entry); null-secondary-data sets $B7 = $FF for every command through C2/1765 except Dance. If all targets are dead when the echo runs it is dropped but the HP cost already applied. The penalty is applied even when the MP check then fails.

astral.hook: C2/31B6 in the per-strike executor C2/317B (see add_steal); prehit C2/2211 only flags MP refresh
astral.trigger: every strike by the holder (physical or magic, healing too), not DoT ticks
astral.effect: $11A3 ^= $80: toggles 'concerns MP' - HP damage/healing becomes MP damage/healing and MP attacks (Rasp, Osmose) become HP attacks. prehit_trigger sets $3204 bit7 on attacker and target at every hit determination so C2/5763 re-greys the spell lists from current MP.
astral.order: after quickening, before vampire (so Astral+Vampire = MP drain)

vampire.hook: C2/31B6 in the per-strike executor C2/317B (see add_steal)
vampire.trigger: every non-healing strike ($11A4 bit0 clear) by the holder, not DoT ticks
vampire.effect: $11A4 |= $02 (drain: damage dealt is absorbed by the attacker, vanilla drain cap rules) and $11A2 |= $08 (reversed on undead targets, like Drain)
vampire.notes: Drain amount then goes through C2/0DEE (ravenous hook).

decisive.hook: C2/2211 (JML main) at the start of the per-target hit determination C2/220D
decisive.trigger: every hit determination where the attacker has decisive
decisive.effect: $341A := 0: the whole current action can no longer be countered - skips BC's counter block (counter_all, hamedo, return_magic, esper_counter, gaia_assist, flinch, discordant, sunken_state) and vanilla counterattacks, and also disables the death triggers (immortal, final_*) of combatants it kills (they require $341A != 0)
decisive.order: after resonate, before the counter block
decisive.vanilla_meaning: C2/220D: hit/miss determination for target Y of attacker X
decisive.notes: patch_junction_hit_trigger is listed for decisive in the manifest but contains no decisive check; its other effects are in patch_junction_damage_trigger (other group).

null_freeze.hook: C2/2211 at the start of hit determination C2/220D
null_freeze.trigger: any attack/spell/item at the holder while it is Frozen ($3EF9 bit1) and its Freeze timer $3F0D,Y != 0
null_freeze.effect: the hit misses (vanilla miss path C2/22D1) before any other check - frozen holder is untouchable (damage, healing, Fire thaw included)
null_freeze.order: very first check of the hit determination, before null_sleep and all counters
null_freeze.notes: Self-targeted actions miss too (e.g. its own fixed-damage commands).

null_sleep.hook: C2/2211 at the start of hit determination C2/220D
null_sleep.trigger: any attack at the holder while it is Asleep ($3EE5 bit7) with its sleep timer $3CF9,Y != 0
null_sleep.effect: the hit misses (C2/22D1), so the sleeper can't be hurt or woken
null_sleep.order: right after null_freeze, before resonate and counters

resonate.hook: C2/2211 at the start of hit determination C2/220D
resonate.trigger: every hit determination where the attacker or the target has resonate (any action, any team, before hit/miss; not if the null_freeze/null_sleep miss already happened)
resonate.effect: Rippler-style swap: statuses the two do not share are exchanged. Bytes 1-2: mask $FD37 (Blind, Zombie, Poison, Clear, Imp, Condemned, Image, Mute, Berserk, Muddled, Seizure, Sleep; never Magitek, Petrify, Wound, Near Fatal). Bytes 3-4: mask $84FE (Regen, Slow, Haste, Stop, Shell, Safe, Reflect, Life 3, Float). E = ~(sX & sY) & mask; target gains sX&E and loses sY&E; attacker gains sY&E and loses sX&E (written to the pending set/clear arrays $3DD4/$3DFC/$3DE8/$3E10, overwriting them).
resonate.order: after null_freeze/null_sleep, before decisive and the counter block
resonate.notes: STA (not ORA) into the pending status arrays may drop other status changes already pending for those two combatants in this strike. Self-target: no change.

flinch.hook: C2/2211 counter block (main-counter) of hit determination C2/220D
flinch.trigger: counterable action ($341A != 0), target is another combatant on the opposite team; 50% (jun-rng1, rolled before the junction check)
flinch.effect: target's ATB high byte $3219,Y := $3219,Y >> 2 (gauge cut to 1/4), unless that would be 0 (then unchanged)
flinch.order: first in the counter block, before counter_all
flinch.notes: Before the hit roll, so misses also flinch. The constant named flinch-rate ($40) is actually counter_all's rate.

counter_all.hook: C2/2211 counter block of hit determination C2/220D
counter_all.trigger: any counterable action ($341A != 0; not decisive) from a combatant on the opposite team (physical or magic, single or multi target; checked per target hit determination, before hit/miss); 25% (jun-rng2 < $40)
counter_all.effect: the holder queues a Fight (command $00, $3A7B 0) at the attacker in its counterattack queue (C2/4EB2), only if the holder can act (living, not Zombie/Petrify/Wound/Berserk/Muddled/Sleep/Stop/Freeze)
counter_all.notes: No guard against countering counterattacks (counters of counters possible). Self-target exclusion compares only the low byte of $3018, so it works for characters only (a monster targeting itself is not excluded; counter_all also needs opposite teams, so no effect here).

discordant.hook: C2/2211 counter block of hit determination C2/220D
discordant.trigger: every counterable action at another combatant (any team; before hit/miss)
discordant.effect: target's battle level $3B18,Y := 10*floor(level/10) + (attacker current HP mod 10); if 0 then 1 (the ones digit of the level becomes the last digit of the attacker's HP)
discordant.notes: BUG: the second division uses 16-bit A whose high byte is left over from HP/10, so when attacker HP >= 2560 the tens part is computed from (hi(HP/10)*256 + level)/10 and truncated to 8 bits. Port the intended formula.

return_magic.hook: C2/2211 counter block of hit determination C2/220D
return_magic.trigger: counterable action ($341A != 0) from another combatant (any team), the current action is not itself a counter-queue action ($B1 bit0 clear), spell-data MP cost $11A5 != 0; character holders need current MP >= $11A5, monsters no MP check. No RNG, no can-act check; before hit/miss/reflect
return_magic.effect: holder queues command $02 Magic with the same spell id ($B6) at the attacker only (counter queue). MP is charged at execution by vanilla: characters pay their own menu cost for that spell (0 if they don't know it), monsters the spell-data cost (vanilla fails the cast if MP is short).
return_magic.notes: A multi-target spell hitting several holders is returned by each. Esper/Lore spell ids are recast through the Magic command. Works on ally casts (including heals) too.

esper_counter.holder: target (characters only: needs an equipped esper)
esper_counter.hook: C2/2211 counter block of hit determination C2/220D; spell picker get-esper-spell (62/0100) from esper_magic_proc
esper_counter.trigger: counterable action from another combatant (any team), holder has an equipped esper; no can-act check; before hit/miss
esper_counter.effect: picks a spell from the holder's equipped esper (see esper_magic: class = ally-type if the attacker is a character, enemy-type if a monster; chance per spell = learn rate / 64, checked from the esper's 5th spell slot upward); if one is picked, queues command $44 (final-attack: Magic animation, no step forward, no name shown) with that spell at the attacker only, MP cost forced 0 ($B1 bit6)
esper_counter.notes: A character hit by an ally (e.g. healed) answers with an ally-type esper spell on that ally. Monster-banned. Same Unicorn-slot quirk as esper_magic.

gaia_assist.holder: either (attacker procs on the target; target procs back on the attacker)
gaia_assist.hook: C2/2211 counter block of hit determination C2/220D
gaia_assist.trigger: counterable action from another combatant, not a spell-proc action itself ($3A7C != $43) and not a DoT tick; rolled separately for the attacker (if it has gaia_assist) then for the target (if it has it): 25% each (jun-rng2 < $40)
gaia_assist.effect: a random step of the battle background's dance (ED/8E5B by $11E2; vanilla odds 7/16, 6/16, 2/16, 1/16) is chosen; if attacker and target are on opposite teams the step must be enemy-type, on the same team it must be ally-type (targeting byte bit1 set and bits 6-7 clear: in vanilla data Sun Bath, Harvester, Kitty, Tapir, Wild Bear, Ice Rabbit); otherwise nothing. The proc queues command $43 (spell-proc) with that step: attacker-holder casts it at the target, target-holder casts it at the attacker. Free, single target, no name shown.
gaia_assist.numbers: 25% per holder per hit determination; then the chosen step (7/16, 6/16, 2/16, 1/16 by slot) must match the needed class, so the real rate is 25% x the summed odds of the fitting steps
gaia_assist.order: after esper_counter, before the physical-only part (sunken_state, hamedo)
gaia_assist.notes: $32E1,Y (current dance of Y) is temporarily overwritten and restored. Uses BC's (possibly randomized) dance tables.

sunken_state.hook: C2/2211 counter block of hit determination C2/220D
sunken_state.trigger: a counterable PHYSICAL ($11A2 bit0) attack from another combatant (any team) at a holder that is not already Clear ($3EE4 bit4); no RNG
sunken_state.effect: auto-casts spell $26 Vanish on itself via command $26 (global special queue, self only, MP 0). The current hit still proceeds normally (Clear arrives after).

hamedo.hook: C2/2211 counter block of hit determination C2/220D
hamedo.trigger: a counterable physical attack using command Fight ($B5 == 0) from another combatant (any team); 50% (jun-rng1)
hamedo.effect: the attack MISSES (vanilla miss path C2/22D1) and the holder queues a Fight at the attacker (counter queue) if it can act; the miss happens even when the holder can't act
hamedo.order: last check of the hit determination prelude; runs before all vanilla evade/Image/Interceptor checks

firestarter.holder: any ally (other than the frozen one) of the combatant being frozen
firestarter.hook: C2/4692 (JSL main-firestarter) in the vanilla Freeze status-set handler C2/4691
firestarter.trigger: whenever Freeze is set on combatant Y (any source), for each other combatant X that can act, is on Y's side and has firestarter
firestarter.effect: X queues command $02 Magic, spell $00 Fire, MP cost forced 0 ($B1 bit6), in its counter queue. Targets: X's whole side (jun-set-target-allies -> $0F party / $3F00 monsters), not just Y: Fire hits every ally with multi-target split. Then the vanilla Freeze timer $3F0D,Y = $22 is set.
firestarter.order: on status application, before the freeze timer is written
firestarter.notes: Probably intended to target only the frozen ally (thaw); as coded it targets the holder's whole team. A frozen null_freeze holder dodges the Fire.

auto_down.holder: any able ally on the same team as the dying combatant (the dying one included)
auto_down.hook: C2/4585 (JSL main) where new status bytes are committed to $3EE4/$3EF8 (C2/43F9 per target)
auto_down.trigger: combatant Y newly gains Wound (bit $0080 not already set). Monster Y: whole routine only 50% of the time (jun-rng1). For each X ($12..0) on Y's team that can act (judged on statuses before this change) and has auto_down
auto_down.effect: X picks the best battle item from the PARTY inventory: items with type&$2F == $26 (battle-usable consumable) whose status word (item data +$15, statuses 1-2) shares a bit with the gained set; an exact match is taken at once, otherwise the one with the most status bits (ties: first in inventory). Party X: 1 is removed from inventory now; monster X: nothing is consumed. X queues command $01 Item with it ($32F4,X = item) at Y (counter queue). Every eligible ally fires (several items can be used).
auto_down.order: Wound checked first; if Wound was gained the zombie/remedy checks see only Wound (stack slot overwritten), so only one category fires per status write
auto_down.vanilla_meaning: C2/4585: write new statuses (Zombie strips some statuses)
auto_down.notes: The dying holder itself qualifies (can-act uses the old statuses); whether its queued Item runs after death depends on the vanilla queue processor. Monsters choose from the player's inventory but don't spend it.

auto_revivify.holder: any able ally on the same team (self included)
auto_revivify.trigger: combatant Y newly gains Zombie ($0002) and did not also gain Wound in the same write; monster Y 50%
auto_revivify.effect: same item logic as auto_down with mask $0002 (e.g. Holy Water); Item command at Y
auto_revivify.order: after the Wound check, before remedy

auto_remedy.holder: any able ally on the same team (self included)
auto_remedy.trigger: combatant Y newly gains any of mask $4865 (Blind, Poison, Imp, Petrify, Mute, Seizure) and gained neither Wound nor Zombie in the same write; monster Y 50%
auto_remedy.effect: same item logic as auto_down with the gained subset (exact match first, e.g. Antidote for Poison, Soft for Petrify; else the item curing the most statuses, e.g. Remedy); Item command at Y

immortal.hook: C2/4606 (JSL main) in the vanilla Wound status-set handler C2/4600
immortal.trigger: holder is getting Wound and wasn't already Wounded, and the killing action is counterable ($341A != 0; e.g. not from a decisive attacker). Every death (no once-per-battle limit).
immortal.effect: holder queues command $44 (final-attack: Magic animation, no step forward, no name, MP 0) with spell $A6 ChokeSmoke (inflicts Zombie, can hit the dead) targeting itself: it rises as a Zombie
immortal.order: first death trigger, then final_spiral, final_esper, final_ripple
immortal.vanilla_meaning: C2/4600: Wound being set - clear pending flags, mark died ($3A56), etc.
immortal.notes: Exact HP/state after Zombie lands on a Wound target is vanilla behaviour (unverified).

final_spiral.hook: C2/4606 in the Wound set handler (see immortal)
final_spiral.trigger: as immortal: every death of the holder by a counterable action
final_spiral.effect: queues command $44 with spell $63 Spiraler (Sabin's blitz: caster sacrifices itself to fully restore allies) with targets = itself as queued; Spiraler's own effect/targeting then applies
final_spiral.notes: Queued target bytes are the holder's own bit; how Spiraler's special effect resolves that is vanilla (unverified).

final_esper.hook: C2/4606 in the Wound set handler (see immortal)
final_esper.trigger: as immortal, but only if not already triggered: characters - their vanilla 'died' bit in $3A56 is not set (it is set right after this hook and cleared when the action's counters are processed, so effectively every death); monsters - TSB on repurposed $3A58 high byte: once per battle per monster slot
final_esper.effect: queues command $40 (junction Summon): character = its equipped esper (none = nothing), monster = random esper 0..26; free; also sets $3204 bit7 (spell-list refresh). Dead summoner does not step forward.

final_ripple.hook: C2/4606 in the Wound set handler; C2/3C2A in vanilla Rippler effect; C2/081F removal cleanup
final_ripple.trigger: as final_esper (characters every death, monsters once per battle), counterable killing action
final_ripple.effect: queues command $44 with spell $9E Rippler at the combatant that last hit the holder ($32E0 via jun-set-target-counter; nobody if invalid/self): Rippler swaps statuses, handing the holder's Wound to the killer. Rippler change (all Ripplers): Wound is removed from the pending statuses of the caster and/or target if that one has instant-death protection ($3AA1 bit2), so it can't kill bosses. Seize fix: when a combatant that has seized someone ($3358,X != $FF) is removed (vanilla cleanup C2/07C8), it queues Magic $DB Discard so the seized character is released.
final_ripple.vanilla_meaning: C2/3C2A: Rippler status swap; C2/081F: end Quick if the removed combatant held it
final_ripple.notes: Rippler uses the vanilla full swap (no mask) apart from the Wound guard.

esper_magic.holder: attacker (characters only: needs an equipped esper)
esper_magic.hook: C2/3250 (JSL main) at the end of each strike, after the vanilla weapon spell-proc check C2/363E
esper_magic.trigger: after a strike by the holder: excluded are free Magic (spell MP $11A5 == 0 and $B5 == $02, i.e. procs) and free self-targeted $B5 == $12 actions; Fight: every strike; other commands: only the last strike ($3A70 == 0)
esper_magic.effect: picks a spell from the equipped esper's list (esper data D8/6E00, 11 bytes: 5 x (learn rate, spell)): wanted class = ally-type if the strike targeted any character ($B8 != 0), else enemy-type; a spell is enemy-type if its targeting byte has $40, or $80/$04 set. r = rand(0..255)>>2 (0..63); from slot 5 down to slot 1, for each matching spell r -= learn rate, the first to go negative is cast. So P(spell) = rate/64 (sum<=64), else no proc. Cast via the vanilla weapon spell-proc path: $3400 = spell, $B2 &= ~$10, $3A70 += 1 -> one extra strike casts it at the same targets for 0 MP.
esper_magic.order: end of strike, after vanilla weapon procs (may overwrite a vanilla/gunblade proc, see gunblade)
esper_magic.vanilla_meaning: C2/3250: show the steal/other message held in $3401
esper_magic.notes: QUIRK: the slot loop's end test compares only the low byte of the offset, so for esper index 23 (Unicorn) only its 5th slot is considered. Monster-banned (and monsters have no equipped esper).

gold_mage.effect: MP is derived from party gold: MP = min(floor(GP/32), 999) (999 if GP >= 65536), max MP 999. Paying cost c: GP -= 32*c (24-bit). Monsters never use gold at C2/32B6 (normal MP); at C2/3F47 (MP-critical) there is no monster check. End of battle MP not saved.
gold_mage.numbers: MP = GP/32 capped 999; cost x32 GP

mp_switch.hook: C2/12F7 (JSL main) in C2/12F5, per-target HP/MP damage application; C2/5402 NOPed (battle-start MP zeroing)
mp_switch.trigger: HP damage (not 'concerns MP') to the holder with current MP != 0, damage != 0 and != $FFFF, damage < current HP (non-lethal only); 50% (jun-rng1); holder has mp_switch and neither blood_mage nor gold_mage
mp_switch.effect: the HP damage is cancelled ($33D0,Y = $FFFF) and the holder queues command $45 fixed damage with value damage | $4000 = the same amount as MP damage to itself (counter queue). If MP is lower the HP damage is still fully cancelled. Also: vanilla's battle-start STZ of current MP for characters without MP commands is removed (max MP is still zeroed), so they keep an MP pool for this.
mp_switch.order: at damage application, after all damage modifiers
mp_switch.vanilla_meaning: C2/12F7: choose HP or MP damage routine by $11A3 bit7; C2/5402: zero MP of characters with no MP commands
mp_switch.notes: prehit_trigger's part for this key is only the spell-list refresh flag ($3204 bit7 on attacker and target at every hit determination). The MP loss arrives as a separate queued action after the current one.

mp_regen.hook: C2/5056 (JSL main) in the damage-over-time command $22 (C2/500B)
mp_regen.trigger: a Regen or Seizure tick (element $11A1 == 0; Poison ticks have element $08 and are untouched)
mp_regen.effect: the tick is based on max MP ($3C30) instead of max HP and $11A3 |= $80 (concerns MP): Regen restores MP, Seizure drains MP, same vanilla tick formula
mp_regen.numbers: vanilla tick formula with max MP
mp_regen.order: replaces the HP base of the tick
mp_regen.vanilla_meaning: C2/5056: tick power from max HP and stamina
mp_regen.notes: Also converts Seizure (and leech-forced) damage ticks to MP. prehit_trigger only adds the spell-list refresh flag ($3204 bit7).

leech.holder: any living combatant on the opposite team
leech.hook: C2/5B74 (JSL main) in the pending-tick processor C2/5B4F; C2/0C98 (JML main-damage) where damage is added to $33D0
leech.trigger: (1) a combatant's Regen/Seizure tick slot comes up (2 of every 8 status-timer ticks) and it has no Regen status and some living enemy holds leech; (2) any DoT tick damage (poison, seizure, leech-forced) to a combatant
leech.effect: (1) it gets a Seizure-type HP damage tick even without Seizure; (2) every living holder on the other side is healed ($33E4) by the full tick damage
leech.numbers: heal = 100% of the DoT damage, per holder
leech.order: replaces the vanilla Seizure/Regen choice for that tick (Regen keeps priority)
leech.vanilla_meaning: C2/5B74: Seizure or Regen pending -> queue command $22; C2/0C98: store accumulated damage
leech.notes: No 9999 cap on the added healing here.

miasma.hook: C2/5AD6 (JSL main) in the per-combatant status-timer tick (C2/5A83 round robin, rate from $3ADD)
miasma.trigger: each status-timer tick of a Poisoned combatant: for every living combatant, a 25% roll (jun-rng2 < $40) and, if that one has miasma, trigger
miasma.effect: the tick's slot is forced to 'poison pending' (index 2), giving an extra Poison tick; vanilla does it 1 tick in 8
miasma.order: after level modulation; replaces that tick's natural slot (a natural Regen/Seizure slot is lost)
miasma.vanilla_meaning: C2/5AD6: dispatch on $3AF0 & 7 (2 = poison pending, 0/4 = regen/seizure pending)
miasma.notes: Holders on either team speed up everyone's poison.

regenerator.trigger: each status-timer tick of a combatant with Regen ($3EF8 bit1) and regenerator, 50% (jun-rng1)
regenerator.effect: the tick's slot is forced to 'regen/seizure pending' (index 0): extra Regen ticks (natural 2 per 8)
regenerator.notes: BUG: if the combatant is Poisoned and no miasma fired, X is 0 after the loop, so the Regen and regenerator checks look at party slot 0 instead. If it also has Seizure, the forced tick is a Seizure tick. initiative patch is another group's.

parts.trigger: once per battle at battle start, every slot (no presence/living check)
parts.effect: queues Regen: $3DE8,X |= $02 (vanilla 'status 3-4 to set' buffer, status-3 bit $02 = Regen), applied by vanilla's next status-application pass.
parts.notes: Normal Regen status (can be dispelled). patch_junction_miasma.txt (another group) also handles regenerator; this part only grants the starting Regen. Exact moment the queued status lands not traced (first status update after battle start).

juggernaut.trigger: every status-timer tick, 50% (rng2-noluck < $80, one roll shared with burst)
juggernaut.effect: battle level $3B18 drifts up from base level (character record $1608 / monster data byte $10): if level <= base -> +1; else +1 with chance 1/(level-base+1); never 100
juggernaut.notes: This patch only does levels; ATB parts are in patch_junction_initiative (other group).

parts.trigger: once per battle at battle start
parts.order: first step of the per-slot routine; Burst (if also held) then multiplies the halved level
parts.notes: Only the level part; patch_junction_miasma.txt (other group) also handles juggernaut. Lower level lowers vanilla's physical/magic damage and level-based effects for the battle.

burst.trigger: every status-timer tick, same 50% roll as juggernaut
