burst.effect: battle level drifts down: if level >= base -> -1; else -1 with chance 1/(base-level+2); never below 1
burst.order: after juggernaut in the same tick

parts.trigger: once per battle at battle start
parts.notes: Only the level part; patch_junction_miasma.txt (other group) also handles burst.

ravenous.holder: drainer (attacker; target if the drain is reversed on undead)
ravenous.hook: C2/0E02 (JSL main) in the drain cap routine C2/0DEE
ravenous.trigger: any HP or MP drain (Drain, Osmose, vampire, ...) by the holder with damage modification on
ravenous.effect: drained amount x1.25 (F0 + F0/4, 16-bit overflow -> $FFFE) and the cap at the drainer's missing HP/MP is removed ($B2 bit7 cleared); the cap at the drainee's current HP/MP stays
ravenous.order: replaces the vanilla drainee cap; the drainer cap after it is skipped for holders
ravenous.vanilla_meaning: C2/0E02: cap drain at target's HP/MP, then at attacker's missing HP/MP
ravenous.notes: For everyone: if the drainee's current HP/MP is 0 and the drainer cap flag is clear, the amount becomes 1 (BC: 'minimum 1 damage for seize').

deaths_door.holder: attacker (any living combatant for the Condemned case)
deaths_door.hook: C2/33BD (JSL main) right after each target's hit determination (C2/33BA JSR $220D)
deaths_door.trigger: an attack with 'miss if death-protected' ($11A2 bit1: Doom, X-Zone, Demi, Quartr, L.5 Doom, Odin, ...) MISSES a target (any reason) and the attacker has deaths_door; or the Condemned countdown's self-Doom (attacker's $3B05 == 1) misses and any living combatant has deaths_door
deaths_door.effect: the target still drops off the hit list but takes fixed damage (no modifiers, $3414 = 0): normal case = attacker MaxHP - current HP (monster attacker /8; negative = heal); Condemned case = 9999
deaths_door.notes: How the display shows a missed target with damage is unverified.

unlimited.hook: C2/15E9 (JSL main) replacing the 1/16 random test of the Desperation Attack check in Fight (C2/15C8)
unlimited.trigger: vanilla gates unchanged (character, $3A3F >= 3, Near Fatal, not Image/Muddled, not Zombie/Clear, a monster targeted)
unlimited.effect: first desperation of the battle: 50% + 50% x 1/16 = 17/32; after one has been used (bit in $3F2F): 25% to clear the bit and fire again (vanilla allows one per battle)
unlimited.order: replaces the vanilla random roll only

final_fenix.holder: the dying Life-3 holder (spec'd in patch_junction_final_fenix, other group)
final_fenix.trigger: queued by patch_junction_final_fenix (other group) with spell $50 Phoenix at the holder's whole side
final_fenix.effect: command $44 runs it: Magic path, no step forward, no name shown, MP 0

parts.holder: the combatant that dies with Life 3 (and, at battle start, each living combatant)
parts.hook: battle start: C2/25FA (same as auto_reraise). Death: C2/07A4 in C2/0799 'Life 3 revival' (JML main replaces LDA #$30 / STA $B8 before vanilla queues self-spell Life)
parts.trigger: battle start: living holder gets Life 3 ($3EF9 |= $04). Later: when the holder is found dead with Life 3 in the post-action death pass (BC's relocated C2/06E3 check calls C2/0799, which first clears Life 3)
parts.effect: instead of vanilla's self-cast of Life ($30), queues BC command $44 (final-attack, from patch_junction_command_final_attack.txt) with spell $50 (Phoenix's summon) targeting the holder's whole team ($B8 = own bit expanded by jun-set-target-allies: all party $0F or all monsters $3F, dead or alive), via jun-queue-command (C2/4EB2).
parts.numbers: spell $50 (Phoenix); command $44; once per battle (Life 3 is consumed and not re-granted)
parts.order: replaces vanilla Life 3 revival; holder itself is among the targets so Phoenix revives it with the rest
parts.vanilla_meaning: C2/0799: remove Life 3, queue spell $30 (Life) on self via C2/4E91 command $26
parts.notes: What Phoenix does (revive all KO'd allies) comes from the spell data and the final-attack command handler (other group). A monster holder casts it on all monster slots.

taunt.holder: each living member of the attacked team (the potential new target)
taunt.hook: C2/58ED in the vanilla target finaliser C2/587E (JML main-target-manipulation, run just before vanilla's JSR C2/522A 'pick one random target bit'); C2/58AF is also rerouted so spreadable/group-capable attacks ($BB & $2C) that ended up with fewer than 2 targets reach C2/58ED too
taunt.trigger: any attack whose target set reaches the 'reduce to one random target' step: single-target attacks ($BB & $2C = 0) with player/AI-chosen targets, spreadable attacks aimed at one target, and auto-targeted attacks (C2/58DE path: $BB & $0C = 0 and, for $BB&$20, vanilla's 50% roll). Skipped while $B2 bit $40 is clear (Runic absorption in progress). Skipped if the attacker is on the attacked team (team-expanded target set contains the attacker's own bit: no Taunt for friendly targeting).
taunt.effect: orig = $B8. Expand to whole team(s) of the targets (party $0F / monsters $3F). For each combatant $12..0 in it: drop if not living (party: dead or Hide; monsters: not in $3A75); a party member is dropped on a 50% roll (jun-rng1) before its Taunt is even checked, then dropped if it lacks Taunt; a monster is kept iff it has Taunt (no roll). If nobody is left: targets unchanged. Monster attacker: targets become all remaining taunters (vanilla then picks one at random). Party attacker: if any original target is among the remaining taunters, targets unchanged; otherwise targets become the taunters (then one picked at random).
taunt.numbers: party-side taunter: 50% per attack to be eligible; monster-side taunter: 100%; final pick uniform among eligible taunters (vanilla C2/522A)
taunt.order: runs first at C2/58ED, then Camouflage, then Salve, then vanilla random pick (C2/58F1 JSR $522A) unless Salve skips it. Multi-target attacks that stay multi-target are never redirected.
taunt.vanilla_meaning: C2/58ED: REP #$20; LDA $B8; JSR $522A (random single target from mask); STA $B8 - collapse a single-target attack's candidate mask to one target. C2/58AF: BEQ $58ED / BRA $58F6 (multi-target capable attacks with a target keep it).
taunt.notes: Holder is the defender-side combatant, the attacker is not checked. For monster attackers a taunter is chosen even when the original target was another taunter (random among taunters). Redirects any attack type (Fight, spells, Steal, items...) that reaches C2/58ED with the attacker on the other team. Party taunters' 50% gate is rolled separately per party member per attack. Living test for party ignores Petrify/Sleep/Vanish etc. (only Wound and Hide exclude). C2/58AF change also means a spreadable spell cast on one target goes through vanilla's single-pick (harmless) and the manipulation.

camouflage.holder: each living member of the attacked team
camouflage.hook: C2/58ED main-target-manipulation (after Taunt), same reroute of C2/58AF as Taunt
camouflage.trigger: same attacks as Taunt (single-target collapse step, attacker on the other team, not during Runic absorption)
camouflage.effect: orig = $B8 (after Taunt). Expand to whole target team(s); remove non-living and every combatant with Camouflage. If nobody is left, or any original candidate is still in the set (i.e. some original candidate lacks Camouflage), targets unchanged. Otherwise (every original candidate has Camouflage) targets become all living non-Camouflage members of that team, and vanilla picks one at random.
camouflage.order: after Taunt, before Salve and the vanilla random pick. If Taunt narrowed targets to taunters who all have Camouflage, Camouflage then redirects away from them to the rest of the team.
camouflage.notes: Only protects when ALL candidates in the mask are camouflaged: a player/AI choosing a camouflaged combatant as its single target is redirected, but a random-target attack whose candidate mask contains anyone without Camouflage is left alone and can still land on the camouflaged combatant (looks like a limitation, not intended protection). If the whole team has Camouflage nothing changes.

sneeze_guard.holder: each combatant on the opposite team from the attacker (Y loop $12..0)
sneeze_guard.hook: C2/5930 in C2/5917 (target-mask cleanup: AND with targetable masks $3A78/$3408/$3403, then if $341A bit7 remove $3F2C jumpers) - JSL main-sneeze-guard replaces LDA $3F2C/TRB $B8
sneeze_guard.trigger: target cleanup of any attack whose status-4 set byte $11AD has bit $20 (inflicts Hide = Sneeze/Snort-style 'remove from battle') and only when $341A bit 7 is set (vanilla's normal case; one special effect at C2/3C8C clears $341A)
sneeze_guard.effect: every opponent of the attacker that has Sneeze Guard is removed from the target mask $B8 (cannot be targeted by the Hide-inflicting attack). Then vanilla: jumpers ($3F2C) removed.
sneeze_guard.order: inside vanilla's target cleanup C2/5917, called from C2/58FA (before auto-targeting/random pick) and from C2/1F51
sneeze_guard.vanilla_meaning: C2/592B-5933: if $341A negative, LDA $3F2C; TRB $B8 - airborne (Jump) combatants are not targetable
sneeze_guard.notes: In vanilla spell data the status-4 bit $20 is set by spells $C2, $CB, $EA (monster Snort/Sneeze-type attacks), $3F, and also $30 Life / $31 Life 2 (lift-status spells) - so an opponent with Sneeze Guard also can't be targeted by Life/Life 2 (e.g. Life used against undead). Same-team check is party(<8) vs monster(>=8), so allies of the attacker with Sneeze Guard can still be targeted. If all targets are removed the attack has no target (vanilla handling of an empty mask). The PR port: filter targets of attacks whose status-set includes Hide/'Remove'.

focus.holder: the party member whose turn it is (party only; X < 8)
focus.hook: C2/0956 (JML main-focus, replaces PEA $B0C2 / PEA $2101 before JSR C2/5864) in the 'does this character get a command menu' check C2/091F; and C2/0926 (JML main-umaro, replaces CMP #berserker / BEQ $08C5)
focus.trigger: each time a party member's ATB fills and vanilla decides between opening the command menu and auto-acting (C2/091F..0960)
focus.effect: (1) Status gate: vanilla opens the menu only if the character has none of Wound/Petrify/Zombie/Sleep/Muddle/Berserk ($3EE4/5 & $B0C2) and none of Dance/Rage/Hide ($3EF8/9 & $2101). With Focus the masks become $80C2 / $2000: Muddle, Berserk, Dance and Rage no longer block the menu - the player inputs commands normally. (2) Permanent berserker (character id = BC parameter berserker-index, $0D Umaro by default; BC picks a random 'umaro_risk' character): vanilla never gives it a menu; with Focus, $3AA0,X |= $02 (controllable) and it continues to the normal menu checks; without Focus/Commander, $3AA0,X &= ~$02 and it auto-acts as vanilla Umaro.
focus.order: berserker check (C2/0926) runs before the $2F4C / seized ($3359) / charmed ($3395) checks; those still block the menu. Status-mask edit runs right before C2/5864.
focus.vanilla_meaning: C2/0926: Umaro ($3ED8 = $0D) never gets a menu. C2/0956: PEA status masks, JSR C2/5864 = carry set if none of the masked statuses -> open menu, else auto-act (C2/0986).
focus.notes: Only the menu gate changes: the statuses stay. A Muddled character with Focus chooses its own targets; vanilla's Muddle side-flip only happens in auto-targeting (C2/597E, when no target was chosen) so player-chosen targets are honoured; auto-targeted commands still flip. Berserk's Fight-only behaviour comes from the skipped auto-act, so a Focused berserker has its full command list. If the berserker's first two command slots are empty ($FFFF) prevent_no_command_softlock puts Fight in slot 1. Monsters never have Focus effects (C2/091F exits for X >= 8).

commander.holder: any OTHER able-bodied party member (slots 0-3, never the acting character itself)
commander.hook: same as focus (C2/0956 check-focus loop; C2/0926 main-umaro loop)
commander.trigger: same as focus: a party member's menu-or-auto decision
commander.effect: the acting character gets the full Focus effect (menu despite Muddle/Berserk/Dance/Rage; permanent berserker controllable) if at least one other party member is able-bodied and has Commander.
commander.numbers: able-bodied = present and alive (in $3A74, no Wound, no Hide) and none of: Petrify, Zombie (status1 $C2 incl. Wound), Sleep, Muddle, Berserk, Mute (status2 $B8), Stop (status3 $10), Frozen, Hide (status4 $22)
commander.order: checked after the actor's own Focus test (Focus short-circuits)
commander.notes: Commander does not help its own holder (loop skips the actor); a Muddled/Berserk/Muted Commander holder stops granting it. Slots tested X = 6,4,2,0.

lucid_dead.hook: C2/0956 main-focus (status masks) and C2/597A (JSL main-lucid-dead, replaces LDA #$40 / TSB $B8 in the auto-target builder C2/5937)
lucid_dead.trigger: menu gate: each time the character's ATB fills. Targeting: when a Zombie party member's attack is auto-targeted (C2/5937 runs when no target was chosen or $BA bit $40 'randomize').
lucid_dead.effect: (1) Zombie ($3EE4 bit $02) no longer blocks the command menu (status1 mask $C2 -> $C0). (2) Vanilla makes a Zombie attacker's auto-targeting pick from both sides ($B8 temp bit $40); with Lucid Dead that is skipped so auto-targets follow the normal side rules.
lucid_dead.order: applied after the Focus/Commander mask edit, before the Highwind edit, all before C2/5864
lucid_dead.vanilla_meaning: C2/5973-597C: if attacker is Zombie, auto-target candidates = both teams
lucid_dead.notes: Zombie's other effects (undead healing inversion, poison-like HP etc.) are untouched. Monsters: check-lucid-dead returns 'no' for X >= 8, so zombie monsters keep vanilla behaviour.

necromancer.holder: any OTHER able-bodied party member (as Commander)
necromancer.hook: C2/0956 and C2/597A via check-lucid-dead's loop
necromancer.effect: the acting character gets the Lucid Dead effect if another able-bodied party member has Necromancer.
necromancer.numbers: able-bodied as for commander (a Zombie Necromancer holder is not able-bodied, so it never helps itself or others while zombied)
necromancer.order: after the actor's own Lucid Dead test
necromancer.notes: Does not affect its own holder.

true_paladin.holder: each potential bodyguard (any eligible combatant other than the target)
true_paladin.hook: C2/1254 in the vanilla cover routine C2/123B (Love Token / True Knight), JML main replacing LDX $336C,Y / BMI $125F
true_paladin.trigger: cover routine runs once per action after targeting (called from C2/32A8) when $B2 bit $02 ('no cover') is clear and there is a target; vanilla clears that bit only in the Fight/Capture command paths (C2/162F, C2/1689, C2/16F9), so effectively Fight/Capture strikes by either side. Target Y = highest-index combatant in $B8 (C2/51F9). Only when the target has no Love Token bodyguard ($336C,Y negative).
true_paladin.effect: candidates = get-potential-bodyguards (see numbers), minus everyone without True Paladin; if any remain, one is chosen uniformly at random (jun-select-bit) and covers: vanilla C2/12C0 + C2/12A8 make it the new target ($B8 = its bit, cover animation). Unlike vanilla True Knight there is NO Near Fatal requirement on the target and no 'highest HP' choice.
true_paladin.numbers: candidate pool: present ($3AA0 bit0), not already covering ($32B8 bit7 set), not seized ($3358 bit7 set), none of Wound/Petrify/Clear/Zombie/Sleep/Muddle ($3EE4/5 & $A0D2), none of Stop/Chant/Hide/Frozen ($3EF8/9 & $3210), living; target excluded. Side: 50% (jun-rng1) the pool is the target's own side only; the other 50% it is both sides IF the target has Popularity, else own side. Own side = party if target is a party member not in $3A42 (acting-as-enemies), else monsters.
true_paladin.order: 1) vanilla Love Token bodyguard ($336C) wins; 2) True Paladin; 3) Popularity; 4) vanilla True Knight relic block (C2/125F onward) still runs but cannot override a cover already made (C2/12A8 requires Y == $F8).
true_paladin.vanilla_meaning: C2/1254: X = Love Token bodyguard of target; if none skip to True Knight check (target must be Near Fatal, not Clear, not seized; highest-HP True Knight wearer on target's side, attacker and target excluded)
true_paladin.notes: The attacker is not excluded from BC's pool (vanilla excludes it), so a paladin attacking its own ally (Muddle) could cover its own strike. With a Popular target, an enemy True Paladin can cover it 50% of the time.

popular.hook: C2/1254 cover routine (after the True Paladin check finds nobody)
popular.trigger: same as true_paladin: a coverable attack (Fight/Capture-type, $B2 bit $02 clear) on the holder when no Love Token bodyguard and no eligible True Paladin
popular.effect: a random eligible combatant from the pool covers the holder (takes the attack instead), every time a pool member exists. Pool as for True Paladin but without the junction filter: 50% own side only, 50% both sides (so enemies of the holder may jump in front of the attack).
popular.numbers: 100% cover if the pool is non-empty; side choice 50/50; uniform pick within the pool
popular.order: after Love Token and True Paladin, before vanilla True Knight (which then cannot override)
popular.notes: Also widens the True Paladin pool to both sides 50% of the time when the target is Popular. If the pool is empty vanilla True Knight is tried.

dog.hook: C2/2282, in hit determination's Interceptor check (JSL main replaces LDA $3EF9,Y / ASL)
dog.trigger: vanilla gates first: command Fight ($B5=$00) or Capture ($06), no special effect ($11A9 = 0), exactly one target ($3EC9 = 1), target is a party member (Y < 8)
dog.effect: if the target has Dog, the Interceptor status bit is treated as set: 50% (C2/4B53) the attack is blocked with the dog animation ($FE = $40, to the miss path C2/22B5); otherwise falls through to vanilla's Golem check ($3A36/$3A37 Golem HP -> block $FE = $20) and the normal hit/evade code.
dog.order: replaces the Interceptor status test only; Golem block, Image and evade come after as in vanilla
dog.vanilla_meaning: if target has Interceptor status ($3EF9 bit $40), 50% block by Shadow's dog
dog.notes: Monsters with Dog get nothing (vanilla gate Y < 8). Only the block is granted; vanilla's Interceptor counterattack is separate code and was not checked - assume Dog does not grant it (unverified).

initiative.hook: C2/25FA, end of each iteration of the battle-start ATB init loop C2/2575 (JML main replaces REP #$20 / DEY / DEY / BPL $2594); patch_junction_esper_defense.txt only supplies check-esper-defense used by the same routine
initiative.trigger: once per battle, for every slot Y = $12..0 (also slots whose vanilla ATB init was skipped: pre-set gauge, $3EE1 special battles, back/pincer attack party)
initiative.effect: after vanilla computed the initial ATB, the holder's $3219,Y (ATB gauge high byte) = $FF: full gauge, acts as soon as the battle starts.
initiative.order: last step of the per-slot battle-start routine: juggernaut -> burst -> regenerator -> auto_reraise/final_fenix -> esper_defense statuses -> plague -> initiative. Overrides vanilla's preemptive/back-attack ATB rules for the holder.
initiative.vanilla_meaning: C2/25FA: next slot of the initial-ATB loop (initial $3219 from Speed + random + slot order, side/back attack rules)
initiative.notes: Applies to monsters with the junction too.

auto_reraise.trigger: once per battle at battle start, if the slot is living (party: in $3A74, no Wound/Hide; monster: in $3A75)
auto_reraise.effect: Life 3 / Reraise status written directly: $3EF9,X |= $04. On death vanilla's Life 3 handling revives the holder once (casts Life $30 on itself, removing Life 3).
auto_reraise.numbers: one revival per battle (status not re-granted)
auto_reraise.order: after regenerator, before esper_defense; Final Fenix grants the same bit
auto_reraise.notes: Direct bit write, no status-set side effects. esper_defense patch is listed only because the shared routine calls its helper.

esper_defense.holder: party member with an equipped esper (party only, Y < 8)
esper_defense.hook: C2/293D (JSL main, in the battle-start per-character stat copy just before $3C58 relic flags) and C2/25FA (initiative main)
esper_defense.trigger: battle start only. Summon spell S = esper id + $36; data = spell table C4/6AC0 + S*14. On BC's always list in summoner mode (espercutegf).
esper_defense.effect: (1) element nullify: $3BCD,Y |= S.element (byte 1) - immune to the summon's element. (2) if S defaults to enemies (byte 0 bit $40) or is a 'lift status' spell (byte 4 bit $04): the statuses S sets (bytes $0A-$0D) are removed from the holder's vulnerability masks $331C/$331D/$3330/$3331 - immune to them. (3) otherwise (ally-side summon that inflicts status): at C2/25FA the holder starts the battle with those statuses: $3EE4/5 |= bytes $0A/$0B, $3EF8/9 |= bytes $0C/$0D with status-4 bit $20 (Hide) forced off.
esper_defense.numbers: none; e.g. Ramuh -> immune to Bolt; Shoat -> immune to Petrify; Carbunkl -> start with Reflect; Phantom -> start with Clear (actual sets come from BC's spell data)
esper_defense.order: (1)(2) during character stat setup (C2/2544 loop), before the ATB loop; (3) in the ATB loop after reraise, before plague
esper_defense.vanilla_meaning: C2/293D: LDA $D8 / STA $3C58,X (relic flags) - re-done by the patch
esper_defense.notes: Status grant is a raw OR (no status-set side effects). Changing espers mid-battle (Caller/summoner mode) does not refresh these. BUG: in initiative main, after check-esper-defense X holds an address (esper RAM pointer or spell offset) and SEP #$30 truncates it, so the following Plague check uses a garbage combatant index for any party member who has esper_defense; port should check the real combatant.

plague.trigger: once per battle at battle start (no living check on the holder)
plague.effect: every combatant on the other team (all 10/4 slots, no presence check) that is not immune to Condemned ($331D bit $01 set) gets $3204,Y |= $20 = vanilla's 'start Condemned countdown' request. At the next force-update (C2/083F, after the first action) C2/09B4 sets its timer $3B05 = max(0, 60 - (L + rand(0..L-1))) + 20 with L = $11AF (attack level of whatever ran last). Vanilla's periodic tick (C2/5AB8) decrements $3B05 while >= 2, without checking the Condemned status; when it reaches 1 the combatant casts Doom ($0D) on itself (C2/5BC7).
plague.numbers: timer 20..80 ticks (80 if L = 0); Doom = vanilla instant death (blocked by death protection)
plague.vanilla_meaning: see initiative; $3204 bit $20 normally set when Condemned status is inflicted
plague.notes: The Condemned status bit itself is NOT set, so the countdown may run without the status icon. Holder-index bug: if the holder is a party member with esper_defense, the junction is checked on a garbage X (see esper_defense). Several Plague holders on one side just set the same flag.

instant_act.holder: the combatant whose command is being queued (party or monster)
instant_act.hook: C2/03F5 in C2/03E4 (set a queued command's wait time: $322C,X = min(CommandWaitTimes[cmd] at C2/067B + $322C,X, $FE)); JSL main replaces TAX / LDA $C2067B,X
instant_act.trigger: every command queued through C2/03E4 (player input, AI, auto actions; commands < $1E)
instant_act.effect: the per-command wait added to $322C is 0 instead of the C2/067B table value: the action starts without the post-input wait.
instant_act.numbers: vanilla waits: Fight/Item/Steal/most $10, Magic/X-Magic/Lore/Health/Shock $20, Morph/Revert 0, Jump $E0 (airtime); Instant Act -> 0 for all
instant_act.order: Highwind's Jump rule is tested first, same result
instant_act.vanilla_meaning: look up the command's wait time and add it to the wait threshold $322C
instant_act.notes: Jump with Instant Act also loses its airtime (lands immediately).

instant_run.hook: C2/5BDB in the periodic run check C2/5BD0 (JML main replaces LDA $3A91 / AND #$70, the 1-in-8 tick throttle)
instant_run.trigger: every timer tick while the player is holding Run (L+R): $2F45 set by the menu (C1/0B73; never set in can't-escape battles, $2F4B bit 0) and $B1 bit $02 clear
instant_run.effect: if any present party member has Instant Run, those members' bits are OR'd into $3A38 (vanilla 'succeeded in running' mask) and control goes straight to C2/5BE2 (if $2F45, $3A38 != 0 and not Colosseum $3A97 = 0: set $B0 bit $04 and queue the escape command $2A). Vanilla's per-character run counters ($3D70 += rand, vs $3A3B) are skipped for the holders. Escape command C2/20DE then removes each flagged runner subject to its vanilla per-character conditions.
instant_run.order: replaces the throttle; if no holder, vanilla throttle and counters as usual
instant_run.vanilla_meaning: only every 8th tick ($3A91 & $70 = 0) check whether anyone's run counter succeeded
instant_run.notes: Only the holders are flagged; others still use the vanilla run counter. Can't-escape battles and the Colosseum still block it.

poach.holder: attacker (party member that lands the killing blow)
poach.hook: C2/13A1 in C2/1390 (HP reached 0 -> set Wound via C2/0E32); JML main replaces LDA #$0080 / JMP $0E32
poach.trigger: a monster (Y >= 8) is killed by HP damage during the Fight command ($B5 = $00 exactly) and the attacker (index taken from the stack, < 8) has Poach; not when the monster is Imp and the attacker has Imp Harvest (that takes over). Zombie targets don't reach this code.
poach.effect: 50% (jun-rng2 bit 0) pick the monster's ROM steal pair (CF/3000 + 4*id: rare, common), else its drop pair (CF/3002: rare, common). Then 32/256 (rng2 < $20) the rare item, else the common. If the chosen slot is $FF nothing happens; otherwise the item is given like a successful Steal: $32F4,attacker = item, $3A8C |= attacker bit (added to inventory after the action), message $3401 = $B0 with $2F35 = item. Then vanilla Wound as normal.
poach.order: at the moment of death, before the Wound status is set; independent of the normal post-battle drop
poach.vanilla_meaning: C2/13A1: LDA #$0080 / JMP $0E32 - inflict Wound on the target whose HP hit 0
poach.notes: Uses ROM item data, so an already-stolen item can still be poached, and the normal end-of-battle drop still happens. No fallback to the other item if the chosen slot is empty. Only Fight kills count (not Jump, spells, Throw...).

imp_harvest.holder: attacker (party member with the killing Fight blow)
imp_harvest.trigger: as Poach, and the killed monster has Imp status ($3EE4 bit $20)
imp_harvest.effect: 50% steal pair / 50% drop pair as Poach, but always the RARE item (byte 0); if $FF nothing. Given like Poach (inventory after the action, message $B0).
imp_harvest.order: checked before Poach; if the monster is Imp and the attacker has Imp Harvest, Poach is not rolled
imp_harvest.notes: If the monster is Imp but the attacker lacks Imp Harvest, Poach is still checked.

freebie.hook: C2/18B0 in the Item/Throw command handler (JSL main replaces LDA #$FF / STA $32F4,X)
freebie.trigger: current command $3A7A = $01 (Item) or $08 (Throw), when vanilla would mark the item as used (only if $B1 bit $10 was clear)
freebie.effect: 25% (jun-rng2 < $40, rolled before the junction check) and holder has Freebie: $32F4,X keeps the item id, so vanilla's end-of-action processing ($3A8C) puts the item back in the inventory = not consumed; battle message $3401 = $B1. Otherwise vanilla: $32F4,X = $FF (consumed).
freebie.order: replaces the consume mark; item effect itself is unchanged
freebie.vanilla_meaning: $32F4,X = $FF: the item taken from inventory at selection is not returned
freebie.notes: Thrown weapons/skeans included. Message $B1 is a BC battle message (text from bcg manifest battle_messages).

gilgam_heart.hook: C2/134A in HP-change routine C2/1323 (after HP -= damage), JML main replaces BEQ $1390 / BCS $133C / BRA $1390
gilgam_heart.trigger: the holder takes net HP damage (damage > healing in the same application) and survives (HP > 0 afterwards)
gilgam_heart.effect: party gold ($1860, 24-bit) += damage taken. Battle message $26 with $2F38 (24-bit) = amount; further Gilgam payouts in the same action add to the shown running total.
gilgam_heart.numbers: 1 GP per HP lost; no cap (gold can pass 9,999,999 - no clamp in the patch)
gilgam_heart.order: after the HP subtraction, before the alive/dead branch; lethal hits pay nothing
gilgam_heart.vanilla_meaning: HP == 0 or borrow -> C2/1390 death, else return alive
gilgam_heart.notes: A monster holder also pays the PARTY when it is hurt. MP damage not counted. Port: clamp gold to the game's max.

double_ap.holder: each living party member at the victory reward step
double_ap.hook: C2/5E2F in the post-battle EXP/AP loop (JSL main before Terra's morph-gauge check); C2/5E77 after the loop (JSL restore-normal-magic-points replaces LDA $F1 / AND $F0 / BEQ)
double_ap.trigger: battle won, formation AP (DF/B400 + formation $3ED4; 0 if formation >= $200) nonzero
double_ap.effect: for a holder, $FB (AP used for this character) = base AP x2, capped at 255, before vanilla uses it for Terra's morph gauge ($1CF6 += $FB*2, Terra only) and esper spell learning/level-up AP (C2/5FEF, C2/602A). Non-holders get base AP. After the loop $FB is reset to base for the 'Got N magic points' message.
double_ap.order: per character inside vanilla's loop, before morph gauge/esper learning
double_ap.notes: Side effect for everyone: the vanilla condition ($F1 & $F0 nonzero) for showing the AP message is removed - the message shows whenever the formation gives AP. Message shows the undoubled amount.

victory_cry.holder: each living party member at the victory reward step
victory_cry.hook: C2/6236 in C2/6235 (add EXP to a character, called from the post-battle loop C2/5E4C/5E56); JSL main replaces REP #$21 / LDA $2F35
victory_cry.trigger: battle won; for each party member alive at that point (loop skips those not in $3A74)
victory_cry.effect: HP = max HP ($3C1C), MP = max MP ($3C30), status bytes 1-2 &= $0030: every status-1/2 ailment removed except Clear ($10) and Imp ($20) (Blind, Zombie, Poison, Magitek, Petrify, Condemned, Near Fatal, Image, Mute, Berserk, Muddle, Seizure, Sleep cleared). Status 3-4 untouched.
victory_cry.order: during EXP gain, before vanilla's level-up processing; dead members get nothing
victory_cry.vanilla_meaning: C2/6235: add battle EXP ($2F35) to the character's EXP
victory_cry.notes: Also clears Magitek status (relevant only in Magitek-armor battles; whether it is written back to the save depends on vanilla's status copy-back mask). Idempotent if C2/6235 runs twice for a character.

vip.hook: C2/06F3 in BC's relocated death pass (patches.py banon_life3 moves vanilla C2/06D8's Banon check after the Life 3 check): JML main replaces LDA $3ED8,X / CMP #$0E / BNE
vip.trigger: post-action death pass (C2/069B per combatant): a party member still Wound after the airborne-Jump save (C2/0710) and Zombie handling, and without Life 3 (monsters branch away earlier)
vip.effect: if the dead character is Banon ($3ED8 = $0E) or has VIP: $3A6E = 6 - battle ends as a loss (vanilla 'Banon fell' game over).
vip.order: after Life 3 (revival takes priority; main re-checks $3EF9 bit $04 too)
vip.vanilla_meaning: Banon dying ends the battle (game over)
vip.notes: The highwind patch makes an airborne Highwind holder's death stand (no landing save), so it can trigger VIP while in the air; that is presumably why highwind lists this patch. Port: if a VIP holder is KO'd without Reraise -> game over.

highwind.holder: the jumper (combatant using Jump $16 or lifted by Palidor)
highwind.hook: C2/21D3 jump-up (main-set-flag), C2/03F5 command wait (instant_act main), C2/0144 queued-Jump execution (main-clear-flag), C2/180B Jump strike (main-jump-command), C2/0956 menu gate (focus main), C2/0B7D Palidor lift (main-palidor), C2/0710 mid-air death (main-sky-die)
highwind.trigger: using the Jump command, being lifted by Palidor, or dying while airborne
highwind.effect: Jump becomes 'hang in the air, land when you choose'. 1) Jump-up: vanilla sets the airborne bit $3F2C (and Hide); for the holder the bit is TOGGLED (set if clear, cleared if already airborne). 2) Jump's wait ($E0 airtime from C2/067B) is 0. 3) Executing the queued Jump: vanilla clears $3F2C and skips if not airborne; for the holder $3F2C is left alone, $3A58 |= its bit (menu refresh) and it always proceeds. 4) Jump strike C2/17F6: holder still airborne -> no strike: battle menu becomes a single Jump command (entry $16,$0B,$43; other 3 slots $FF), $3E4D bit $40 set, return; holder not airborne (second Jump toggled the bit off) -> $3E4D bit $40 cleared, commands reloaded (C2/532C), then the vanilla landing strike. 5) While airborne the holder may open the menu despite Hide (focus patch removes Hide from the gate mask when in $3F2C). 6) Palidor (C2/0B4A, airborne via $3204 bit 0): $3E4D |= $40, Jump-only menu, $3A58 |= bit, wait $322C = 0 instead of $E0, and the next queued entry after the head ($3184 link from $32CC) has its command changed to $15 (Def.) - it then hangs like a normal Highwind jump. 7) Death while airborne: vanilla converts it to 'dies on landing' (clears Wound, Air-Anchor style); for an airborne holder this is skipped, so it dies at once (and VIP/Banon game-over can fire).
highwind.numbers: airtime 0 both ways; no limit on time spent airborne
highwind.order: first Jump = leave + immediate 'landing' with no strike; each later turn the menu offers only Jump; choosing it lands immediately with the vanilla Jump strike (weapon, Dragon Horn extra jumps etc. unchanged) and restores the normal menu
highwind.vanilla_meaning: Jump: airborne for $E0 wait, untargetable (jumpers removed from target masks), then a single landing strike
highwind.notes: Untargetable while hanging (vanilla removes $3F2C combatants from targets when $341A bit 7). ATB keeps refilling while airborne. C1/4849/C1/4855 addresses are declared but not hooked. A monster holder using Jump would get its 'menu' written at $202E + slot*12 (outside the party menu) - edge case.

maintenance.holder: enemy GP theft: the party member being robbed (target); Ogre Nix: combatant Y of the weapon effect (the wielder per BC's label)
maintenance.hook: C2/3A0C in the Steal effect's monster-steals-GP branch (C2/3A09); C2/3EE4 in the Ogre Nix weapon effect (break roll)
maintenance.trigger: a monster uses its GP-stealing Steal on the holder; the holder attacks with Ogre Nix
maintenance.effect: GP theft: the 75% success roll (vanilla rand < $C0) is forced to fail (A = $FF) - no GP stolen. Ogre Nix: the break roll (vanilla rand(0..HP/10) == 0 -> weapon $17 removed from the hand, message $44) is forced to 'no break'.
maintenance.vanilla_meaning: C2/3A0F: rand >= $C0 -> theft fails; C2/3EE4: rand(N) - 1 >= 0 -> weapon survives
maintenance.notes: Non-holders' rolls now use jun-rng2/jun-rng3 (same C0/FD00 table driven by $BE as vanilla C2/4B5A/4B65). Exact owner of HP in the Ogre Nix roll (wielder vs target) not re-verified; BC treats Y as the wielder.

innate_runic.hook: C2/353E in C2/352B (Runic absorber scan), JML main replaces LDA $3E4C,Y / BIT #$06 / BEQ
innate_runic.trigger: any spell with $11A3 bit $08 ('can be Runicked') being cast, by anyone
innate_runic.effect: the holder counts as being in Runic stance (vanilla $3E4C bits $02/$04) for every runic-able spell: if it also passes vanilla's status gate (no Wound/Petrify, Sleep, Stop, Frozen, Hide) it is added to the absorber set $EE; vanilla then has an absorber soak the spell (spell nullified, MP gained = spell's MP cost). The stance is never consumed.
innate_runic.numbers: permanent; vanilla absorber choice and MP gain
innate_runic.vanilla_meaning: only combatants who used Runic (bit $04, cleared here = one use) or have the $02 Runic flag absorb
innate_runic.notes: Absorbs allies' runic-able spells too (vanilla Runic is side-blind), e.g. party Cure spells. Works for monsters with the junction.

caller.holder: the character whose battle Magic menu is open ($7E62CA) / the summoner (slot X)
caller.hook: battle spell-list build C2/5789 (main-multicast, replaces TYX / SEC before BIT $3F2E); battle menu C1/82C1 (main: Left/Right on the esper line), C1/82D6, C1/82AD; C2/5429 (Magic availability)
caller.trigger: each time the battle magic list is built; pressing Left or Right (not with Down) in the battle Magic menu
caller.effect: (1) Multi-summon: vanilla greys the esper entry once the character has summoned this battle ($3F2E); a holder's esper entry is just MP-checked, so it can summon again and again. (2) Esper switching: Left/Right cycles the equipped esper through BC's fixed order (ids 0E 0D 07 13 0F 18 16 01 11 06 0B 09 14 1A 10 0C 00 02 05 03 15 19 08 04 0A 17 12, then 'none' $FF; wraps), skipping espers that are not owned ($1A69 bits), not allowed for this character by BC's esper-allocation table, or equipped by any other character record (all 16). The new esper is written to $3344,slot AND the save ($161E of the character record - persists after battle); the menu entry gets its MP cost (C4/6DB9 + id*14; Economizer -> 1, else Gold Hairpin -> (cost+1)/2) and targeting, and is greyed if 'none', Imp, or MP < cost; the esper name is redrawn.
caller.numbers: no summon-count limit; MP cost per vanilla relic rules
caller.order: menu-side only for switching; multi-summon at spell-list build
caller.vanilla_meaning: C2/5789: esper entry disabled if bit in $3F2E (already summoned); C1/82C1: menu confirm handling
caller.notes: Side effects for everyone (no junction check): C2/5429 now always keeps Magic/X-Magic in the battle menu (vanilla blanks it when the character has no spells and no esper, $F6 = 0 and $F7 = $FF); C1/82D6 refuses A on a greyed esper entry. Junctions of the new esper apply immediately (checker reads $161E live) but battle-start esper effects (esper_defense) are not re-run. On BC's always list in summoner mode.

junction_jammer.effect: a random living combatant (characters and monsters, $3A74 bits) is picked; if it has Junction Jammer, the check fails
junction_jammer.numbers: P(fail) = holders among the living / living
junction_jammer.order: after the holder's own lists and blacklists
junction_jammer.notes: Read by bc-junction from patch_junction_core.txt (jun-checker-wrapper). Each check rolls separately.

patch_junction_damage_modification.txt.holder: n/a (no junction of its own / shared code)
patch_junction_damage_modification.txt.hook: C2/336F (JML main; main re-executes the replaced LDA $11A2 / LSR and returns to C2/3373). Per-strike combat routine (C2/3292 path), X = attacker, $11B0 = this strike's base damage/healing (from C2/2B9D), $11A1 = attack elements. Runs after Morph's $BC+=2, before Berserk's $BC+=1.
patch_junction_damage_modification.txt.trigger: every strike that reaches C2/336F (damage and healing actions alike: $11B0 is also the healing base); once per strike, not per target
patch_junction_damage_modification.txt.effect: damage_modification order (all on $11B0, once per strike): 1 EspAtk adds esper elements to $11A1; 2 for each element in $11A1 in order Fire, Ice, Bolt, Bio, Wind, Pearl, Earth, Water: attacker's <elem> Boost x1.5, then x1.25 per living <elem> Font holder, then x0.75 per living <elem> Sink holder; 3 Summon Boost; 4 Nuke Boost/Font/Sink; 5 Phys Boost/Font/Sink; 6 Loner; 7 Crisis Arm; 8 Gaia Boost; 9 Atma Force. Then vanilla: Berserk $BC+1, multi-target split /2 (C2/337E), back-row /2 (C2/3392), special-effect pre-hook C2/3E7D, hit checks, crit ($BC+2, Crit Boost), $11B0 x(1+$BC/2) at C2/341C, then per target C2/0B83 (variance, defense, Safe/Shell, elements w/ pierce), then damage_trigger.
patch_junction_damage_modification.txt.numbers: x1.5 = d + floor(d/2), saturating at 65535; x1.25 = d + floor(d/4), saturating at 65535; x0.75 = floor(d/2) + floor(d/4); every step floors; multiplicative in the order given
patch_junction_damage_modification.txt.vanilla_meaning: C2/336F: physical attack ($11A2 b0) by a Berserk attacker ($3EE5 b4) -> $BC += 1 (+50%). Unchanged, runs after main.
patch_junction_damage_modification.txt.notes: Element/Nuke/Phys/Summon/Loner/Crisis/Gaia/Atma all modify $11B0 before the multi-target split and before the special-effect pre-hook (C2/33A6 -> C2/3E7D): damage that a special effect sets later (e.g. Revenge's maxHP-curHP) gets none of them; %-of-HP attacks ($11A4 b7 -> C2/0D87) don't use $11B0 at all. Loner/Crisis Arm/Gaia/Atma/Summon also scale healing. Final per-target damage is still capped at 9999 by vanilla (C2/0C95) and by damage_trigger. The esper elements stay ORed into $11A1 for the rest of the strike (they then also count for target weakness/absorb, ForceField, Freeze-thaw etc.). Also contains the helpers boost-damage-half/quarter, reduce-damage-quarter at 62/0E00, 62/1440, 62/1460 (reused by reflect_boost) and calls vanilla C2/47B7 (24-bit multiply) and C2/B8F3 (16-bit divide) for Atma Force.

Meatbone/Auto-Potion write $B8/$B9 and $3A7A/$3A7B mid-loop; combatants processed later in the same loop (lower Y) see those clobbered values (affects Precision's target count and Catch's $3A7A test). patch_junction_command_expansion.txt.hook: C2/13FC and C2/155B command jump-table dispatches
patch_junction_command_expansion.txt.effect: Replaces both command dispatches: command id < $34 -> vanilla handler (bank C2, same table copied to 61/F100); id >= $34 -> handler address from 61/F100 + 2*id in bank $62. New ids: $40 summon (61/F180), $41 jump, $42 custom-MP spell, $43 spell-proc, $44 final-attack, $45 fixed-damage. Handlers end by JML into vanilla C2 code that RTSes back to C2/1401 (the normal post-command sequence: counters C2/4C5B, state update C2/083F, ...). QUEUE SEMANTICS: jun-queue-command = vanilla C2/4EB2: entry added to the actor's counterattack queue ($32CD,X, actor listed in $3920); queue-time MP cost (C2/4F08) is 0 for all commands >= $34 and for any command queued with $B1 bit6 set. The main loop (C2/0019) runs the global special queue $340A first, then the $3920 counter list (C2/4B7B), then normal turns; both run with $B1 bit0 set, so vanilla counterattack scripts (C2/4C5B) and BC's return_magic ignore them, while BC's other prehit reactions (counter_all, hamedo, esper_counter, gaia_assist, flinch, discordant, sunken_state, resonate) can still respond because $341A is reset to $FF at every command start (C2/13F2). The queue processor does not require the actor to be alive (final attacks from dead actors are intended).
patch_junction_command_expansion.txt.vanilla_meaning: C2/13FC: JSR ($19C7,X) run command; C2/155B: JMP ($19C7,X) re-dispatch after spell->command conversion (C2/1DBF)
patch_junction_command_expansion.txt.notes: Port: register six new internal command ids; they never appear in menus.

patch_junction_command_summon.txt.hook: command $40 (handler 62/8180, table 61/F180); re-enters vanilla C2/175F (Magic/Lore path)
patch_junction_command_summon.txt.effect: Actor X: monster -> esper = random 0..26 (jun-rng3 $1B); character -> its equipped esper ($161E of its record), none ($FF) -> no action (RTS C2/151E). Spell $B6 = esper + $36 (Ramuh $36 .. Phoenix $50); $B5 = $02 (cast through the Magic path, esper spell id -> esper animation/effect); targets $B8/$B9 = 0 so vanilla default/auto targeting of that esper spell applies; $3415 = 0; if the actor is not alive the step-forward is suppressed ($B0 &= ~$10). MP: 0 (queue cost 0; spell-data cost only lands in $11A5). Shows the spell name. Countering: see queue semantics in command_expansion; reflection per the esper spell's own flags (most espers unreflectable).
patch_junction_command_summon.txt.vanilla_meaning: C2/175F: load spell $B6, run strike (Magic/Lore entry)

patch_junction_command_jump.txt.hook: command $41 (handler 62/8040, table 61/F182); ends in vanilla C2/4ECB
patch_junction_command_jump.txt.effect: Re-queues the actor: $3A7A = $16 Jump, actor appended to the $3820 ready-to-act list, targets = combatant that last hit the actor ($32E0,actor & $7F, if < 10 and not itself; else none -> vanilla retarget), then C2/4ECB adds it to the actor's NORMAL queue ($32CC). The actor then performs a vanilla Jump (leaves the field, untargetable, lands on the target later). MP 0. A physical Fight-type attack when it lands: counterable/not reflectable as vanilla Jump.
patch_junction_command_jump.txt.vanilla_meaning: C2/4ECB: append command to a combatant's normal action queue
patch_junction_command_jump.txt.notes: $3A7B is a leftover (vanilla Jump ignores it).

patch_junction_command_custom_mp_spell.t.effect: If none of the queued targets $B8/$B9 is alive -> no action (RTS C2/00E3). Else $B5 = $02, $3A4C (MP to deduct at end of strike, C2/32B1) = $11A5 = $B7 (the Quickening cost left in $B7 by hit_trigger), $B7 = $FF, then the vanilla Magic path casts spell $B6 (= queued $3A7B, the original spell) at the original targets with normal animation and name. Not enough MP at the end -> vanilla 'not enough MP' failure. Reflectable / dodgeable per the spell's data; it can itself trigger Quickening again (chain). Counters: see command_expansion queue semantics.
patch_junction_command_custom_mp_spell.t.notes: Shows name; counterable/reflectable per spell data.

patch_junction_command_spell_proc.txt.hook: command $43 (handler 62/8120, table 61/F186); jumps straight to the strike executor C2/317B
patch_junction_command_spell_proc.txt.effect: Requires the actor alive and at least one queued target alive (else RTS). $B6 = $3A7D (queued spell), loads spell data (C2/274D) and damage setup (C2/2951), $B5 = $02 (Magic animation), targeting byte $BB = ($11A0 & $40) | $03 (single target, keeps enemy-default bit), $BA |= $04 (no retarget if the target is invalid), $BA &= ~$40 (no random target), $B0 &= ~$10 (no step forward), $B2 &= ~$01 (attack name hidden). Bypasses C2/175F, so $B7 is not reset. MP 0 (queued cost 0; no deduction). Reflection/dodge per the spell data (dance steps). Hits made by it never trigger gaia_assist (main-gaia skips $3A7C == $43).
patch_junction_command_spell_proc.txt.notes: Its hits can't trigger gaia_assist again.

patch_junction_command_final_attack.txt.trigger: queued by esper_counter, immortal, final_spiral, final_ripple, final_fenix
patch_junction_command_final_attack.txt.effect: $B5 = $02 (Magic animation), $B0 &= ~$10 (actor does not step forward, so a dead actor stays down), $B2 &= ~$01 (no attack name), then the Magic path casts queued spell $B6 at the queued targets. MP 0 (queue cost 0, never deducted). Reflectable/dodgeable per the spell's data. Works for dead actors. Spells used: esper spells (esper_counter), $A6 ChokeSmoke (immortal), $63 Spiraler (final_spiral), $9E Rippler (final_ripple), $50 Phoenix (final_fenix).

patch_junction_command_fixed_damage.txt.hook: command $45 (handler 62/8200, table 61/F18A); jumps into vanilla C2/3292 (per-target hit/damage/apply part of the strike, skipping damage calculation)
patch_junction_command_fixed_damage.txt.effect: Actor hits ITSELF only ($B8 := own bit, $11A0 = $03, $BA = $04 no retarget) for exactly ($B8 & $3FFF) as queued: bit $4000 -> MP damage ($11A3 |= $80), bit $8000 -> healing ($11A4 |= $01). Setup: $B5 = $12 (no battle animation), $B3 &= ~$80 (ignore Clear), $3414 = 0 (no damage modification: no defense, Safe/Shell, row, variance), $11A5 = 0 (no MP), element none, power 1, hit/special/status bytes 0, $11A2 = $60 (ignore defense, no split), $11A3 = $02 (unreflectable), $11A4 = $20 (can't be dodged). Still passes through hit determination (C2/220D), so a frozen null_freeze / asleep null_sleep actor dodges it; self-target so no counters.
patch_junction_command_fixed_damage.txt.vanilla_meaning: C2/3292: hit determination loop, damage application, MP deduction for the strike
